description: Everything that drives AutoCAD from outside the user interface: plain script files and the headless Core Console, the loaders that bring AutoLISP, .NET and ObjectARX code into a session, the COM/ActiveX object model used from VBA and Python, the managed .NET API used by add-ins and by cloud Design Automation, and the macro layer behind ribbon buttons, action macros and command aliases. The entries are ordered from the simplest layer (a text file of keystrokes) to the deepest (C++ and server-side automation), and note for each one where it works: interactive AutoCAD, accoreconsole.exe, or Autodesk Platform Services.

tools.name: .scr script file
tools.description: A script is a plain ASCII text file whose every line is typed at the command prompt exactly as a user would type it, replayed by the SCRIPT command, the acad.exe /b switch or accoreconsole /s. It is the lowest-friction automation layer in AutoCAD: no compiler, no API, no licence beyond the product itself. Scripts are strictly linear - they cannot branch, loop or test anything - so conditional work belongs in AutoLISP or .NET that the script loads and calls. The whole file runs in the drawing that is current when it starts, and any error or Esc stops it where it stands.
tools.usage:
; purge_audit.scr  - one command-line response per line
FILEDIA
0
_-PURGE
_All
*
_N
_QSAVE

; run it
SCRIPT  C:\batch\purge_audit.scr
acad.exe /b "C:\batch\purge_audit.scr"
accoreconsole.exe /i in.dwg /s "C:\batch\purge_audit.scr"

parameters.name: blank line
parameters.description: A blank line is an Enter keypress. Commands that end with an extra Enter therefore need an extra empty line, and a trailing blank line at the end of the file is significant - leaving it out is the most common reason a script stops one keystroke short.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description: A space inside a line is also an Enter/accept at most prompts, so responses can be written either one per line or space-separated on one line. This is why file names containing spaces must be wrapped in double quotes.

parameters.name: ; comment
parameters.description: A line whose first character is a semicolon is ignored, which is the only form of documentation a script supports. A semicolon elsewhere is not a comment.

parameters.name: _ prefix
parameters.description: An underscore before a command or option name forces the English (global) name, so the script survives a localised AutoCAD installation: _-LAYER, _ZOOM, _E.

parameters.name: - prefix
parameters.description: A hyphen selects the command-line version of a command that would otherwise open a dialog: -INSERT, -LAYER, -PURGE, -HATCH, -PLOT, -WBLOCK. Combine both prefixes as _-INSERT.

parameters.name: . prefix
parameters.description: A leading period runs the built-in definition of a command even if an alias or a LISP redefinition has replaced it, as in _.LINE. Standard practice in macros and third-party-heavy environments.

parameters.name: FILEDIA / ATTDIA
parameters.description: Set both to 0 at the top of the script so no file or attribute dialog can appear and swallow input, and restore them at the end.

parameters.name: file encoding
parameters.description: Plain ASCII/ANSI text with a .scr extension. Unicode text with a byte-order mark can fail on the first line, and the file should end with a newline.

tools.example:
; issue_set.scr - clean, audit, zoom and plot every drawing it is run against
; called as: accoreconsole /i "%%F" /s issue_set.scr /isolate
FILEDIA
0
ATTDIA
0
ATTREQ
0
EXPERT
2
_-PURGE
_All
*
_N
_AUDIT
_Y
_ZOOM
_E
_-LAYER
_S
0

_QSAVE
tools.notes: A script cannot answer a dialog, a grip edit or an in-place editor, so -MTEXT, -HATCH, -INSERT and friends are mandatory. RSCRIPT restarts the current script, RESUME continues one that was interrupted, and DELAY pauses it. SCRIPTCALL controls whether one script may call another. Anything that needs an if or a loop should be a LISP file loaded by the script with (load "tools.lsp") and then called as a command.

tools.name: SCRIPT
tools.description: Run a script file in the current drawing. The command opens the Select Script File dialog, or prompts for a name on the command line when FILEDIA is 0, then feeds every line of the file to the command processor as if typed. Playback stops on the first error and on Esc, leaving the drawing in whatever state it reached, which is why batch work is usually done on copies or under accoreconsole rather than interactively.
tools.usage:
SCRIPT  (alias SCR)
Select Script File dialog

; script-safe form
FILEDIA
0
SCRIPT
C:\batch\purge_audit.scr

parameters.name: script file
parameters.description: Path to the .scr file. The extension may be omitted; paths with spaces need double quotes.

parameters.name: FILEDIA
parameters.description: 0 replaces the file dialog with a command-line prompt, which is what lets one script start another or a macro start a script.

parameters.name: SCRIPTCALL
parameters.description: System variable controlling whether a SCRIPT command inside a running script is honoured (1) or ignored (0, the legacy behaviour that prevented nested scripts).

parameters.name: Esc
parameters.description: Interrupts playback at the current line; RESUME continues from there.

parameters.name: current drawing
parameters.description: The script runs against whatever drawing is open. A script that must process a specific file should OPEN it first, or be launched with accoreconsole /i.

tools.example:
; From a CUI macro button
^C^C_FILEDIA;0;_SCRIPT;C:/batch/plot_current.scr;

; From AutoLISP
(setvar "FILEDIA" 0)
(command "_.SCRIPT" "C:/batch/plot_current.scr")

; Chained scripts (needs SCRIPTCALL = 1)
; first.scr
SCRIPTCALL
1
_SCRIPT
C:/batch/second.scr
tools.notes: A script started with SCRIPT runs inside the current session, so profile settings, loaded applications and the current layer all still apply. Errors are silent in the sense that playback simply halts; log what matters by writing to a file from LISP or by redirecting accoreconsole output instead.

tools.name: RSCRIPT
tools.description: Repeat the script that is currently running, or the last one that ran, from its first line. Placed as the final line of a .scr file it turns the script into an infinite loop, which is the classic way to build an unattended slide show, a demonstration loop on a trade-stand machine or a polling routine that reloads an xref at intervals. Esc is the only way out.
tools.usage:
RSCRIPT

; typical looping script
VSLIDE
slide1
DELAY
3000
VSLIDE
slide2
DELAY
3000
RSCRIPT

parameters.name: (no arguments)
parameters.description: RSCRIPT takes no input; it simply restarts the current script file.

parameters.name: placement
parameters.description: Only meaningful as the last line of a script. Anywhere else it still restarts from line 1, which usually means an unintended loop.

parameters.name: Esc
parameters.description: The only supported way to break the loop in an interactive session.

parameters.name: DELAY
parameters.description: Almost always paired with RSCRIPT so the loop does not consume the machine.

tools.example:
; watch.scr - reload xrefs every 30 seconds on a site display
_-XREF
_R
*
DELAY
30000
RSCRIPT
tools.notes: Never put RSCRIPT in a script that will run under accoreconsole: the console has no user to press Esc and the work item or batch job will run until it is killed or times out.

tools.name: DELAY
tools.description: Pause a running script for a given number of milliseconds. Its original purpose was slide shows, where each image has to stay on screen long enough to be read, but it is also the pragmatic fix for scripts that race ahead of a slow operation such as an xref reload, a plot spool or a network file becoming available. The maximum single delay is 32767 milliseconds, so longer waits need several DELAY lines.
tools.usage:
DELAY <milliseconds>

DELAY
2000        ; two seconds

; ten seconds, because 32767 ms is the per-call maximum
DELAY
32767
DELAY
32767

parameters.name: milliseconds
parameters.description: 0 to 32767. Values above the maximum are rejected; values are approximate because the delay is measured against the system timer.

parameters.name: script context
parameters.description: DELAY is only useful inside a script; typed at the prompt it simply blocks the session for the given time.

parameters.name: VSLIDE / VSLIDE *
parameters.description: The slide-show partner commands - VSLIDE displays a .sld file and VSLIDE * preloads the next one during the delay.

tools.example:
; show three slides for three seconds each, then loop
VSLIDE
C:/slides/plan
DELAY
3000
VSLIDE
C:/slides/elevation
DELAY
3000
VSLIDE
C:/slides/section
DELAY
3000
RSCRIPT
tools.notes: DELAY is a blocking wait, not a yield: AutoCAD does nothing else during it. Under accoreconsole every DELAY is dead time added to the batch, so remove them from headless scripts unless they are genuinely waiting on an external process.

tools.name: RESUME
tools.description: Continue a script that was interrupted by Esc or by an error, starting at the line after the one that stopped it. It can be issued transparently with a leading apostrophe, so a user can cancel a running script, fix something by hand, and then let the rest of the script carry on. It is the only recovery mechanism scripts have, since they cannot trap errors themselves.
tools.usage:
RESUME
'RESUME        ; transparent form, from inside another command

parameters.name: (no arguments)
parameters.description: RESUME takes no input. It resumes the most recently interrupted script in the current session.

parameters.name: 'RESUME
parameters.description: Transparent invocation, usable while another command is active.

parameters.name: interruption point
parameters.description: Playback continues from the line following the interruption, so a partly-typed command must be finished or cancelled by hand first.

parameters.name: Esc
parameters.description: The interruption RESUME is designed to undo; a second Esc while paused does not abandon the script, it merely does nothing.

tools.example:
; Script stops because a layer name was wrong.
; The user fixes it at the prompt:
-LAYER
M
DIM-TEXT

; and then hands control back to the script:
RESUME
tools.notes: There is no RESUME in the Core Console: a headless script that fails simply ends the session. Design batch scripts so each step is independent and idempotent, and rerun the whole drawing rather than trying to resume it.

tools.name: accoreconsole.exe
tools.description: The AutoCAD Core Console: a command-line executable that hosts the drawing engine and the command processor with no graphical subsystem at all. It loads one drawing, replays a script against it, writes its command-line output to stdout and exits, which makes it the supported way to process thousands of DWGs from a batch file, a service or a scheduler. It starts in a second or two rather than the half minute a full AutoCAD session needs, and the same engine is what Autodesk runs server-side for Design Automation.
tools.usage:
accoreconsole.exe /i <input.dwg> /s <script.scr> [/l <language>] [/isolate] [/product <key>]

; default install location
"C:\Program Files\Autodesk\AutoCAD 2025\accoreconsole.exe"

parameters.name: /i <drawing>
parameters.description: Input drawing to open. Omit it and the console starts on an empty drawing based on the default template, which is how scripts that build a DWG from nothing are run.

parameters.name: /s <script>
parameters.description: Script file to replay. Every line is fed to the command processor exactly as SCRIPT would feed it.

parameters.name: /l <language>
parameters.description: Language pack to load, for example en-US. Matters when the machine has several language packs and the script uses localised command names - though a script written with _ prefixes does not care.

parameters.name: /isolate
parameters.description: Copy the user registry product key for this instance so profile and system-variable changes made by the script stay inside the console session and never reach the interactive product. Use it in every batch run.

parameters.name: /product <key>
parameters.description: Choose which vertical's registry settings and command set to load - ACAD, ACADM (Mechanical), ACADE (Electrical) and so on - on a machine hosting several AutoCAD-based products.

parameters.name: stdout
parameters.description: Everything the command line would have printed goes to standard output, so redirecting it with > or >> gives a per-drawing log without any extra code.

parameters.name: no GUI
parameters.description: There is no window, no dialog engine and no display list. Dialog commands, OLE, rendering, some plotting paths and anything that needs a device context are unavailable; .NET is the API to write against here.

tools.example:
accoreconsole.exe /i "D:\Projects\1042\A-101.dwg" /s "C:\batch\purge_audit.scr" /isolate > "C:\batch\logs\A-101.log" 2>&1

; script that loads a .NET command and calls it
; extract.scr
FILEDIA
0
NETLOAD
C:\bundles\Extractor.dll
EXTRACTTAGS
C:\out\A-101.json
_QSAVE
tools.notes: Drawings opened by the console are opened for write, so the file must not be locked by an interactive session. Plotting to a system printer generally fails here because there is no display subsystem; plot to a .pc3 such as DWG To PDF where it is supported, or do the export from a full AutoCAD session started with acad.exe /b. Design Automation activities add /al to point the console at an uploaded AppBundle.

tools.name: acad.exe
tools.description: The full AutoCAD executable accepts a drawing name followed by switches that control what it opens, which profile and workspace it starts in, what it loads and what it runs. Starting AutoCAD this way is heavier than the Core Console - it needs a licence seat, a display and roughly half a minute - but it is the route for work the console cannot do, such as plotting through a system printer driver, rendering, or anything that depends on the graphics subsystem. The drawing name must come first; switches follow in any order.
tools.usage:
acad.exe ["drawing.dwg"] [/t "template.dwt"] [/b "script.scr"] [/nologo] [/p "profile"]
         [/s "folder;folder"] [/ld "app.arx|app.dbx"] [/w "workspace"] [/v view] [/pl "set.dsd"]

parameters.name: /b <script>
parameters.description: Run a script after startup, in the drawing named on the command line or in the new drawing created from the template. Put it last so the session is fully configured before playback starts.

parameters.name: /t <template>
parameters.description: Start a new drawing from the named .dwt instead of opening an existing file.

parameters.name: /nologo
parameters.description: Suppress the splash screen, which also removes the focus steal that can break the first lines of a script.

parameters.name: /p <profile>
parameters.description: Start with a named user profile, or with a profile previously exported to an .arg file. Isolates support paths, printer settings and system variables from the user's normal profile.

parameters.name: /s <folders>
parameters.description: Append one or more semicolon-separated folders to the support file search path for this session only, without editing the user's Options.

parameters.name: /ld <module>
parameters.description: Load an ObjectARX (.arx) or DBX (.dbx) module at startup, before the drawing opens.

parameters.name: /w <workspace> and /v <view>
parameters.description: /w restores a named workspace (ribbon and palette arrangement); /v restores a named view saved with VIEW once the drawing is open.

parameters.name: /pl <dsd>
parameters.description: Publish a Drawing Set Description file produced by PUBLISH in the background, without opening the drawings interactively.

tools.example:
"C:\Program Files\Autodesk\AutoCAD 2025\acad.exe" /t "C:\standards\A1.dwt" /nologo /p "BATCH" /s "C:\standards\blocks;C:\standards\fonts" /b "C:\batch\build_sheet.scr"

; plot a saved sheet set in the background
"C:\Program Files\Autodesk\AutoCAD 2025\acad.exe" /pl "D:\Projects\1042\IssueC.dsd"
tools.notes: Quote every path that contains spaces, including the path to acad.exe itself. A /b script that ends without QUIT leaves the session open - end batch scripts with _QSAVE then _QUIT (or _CLOSE) so the process exits. Only one instance per licence seat, so acad.exe does not parallelise the way accoreconsole does.

tools.name: accoreconsole batch loop (.bat)
tools.description: The standard pattern for processing a folder tree of drawings: a Windows batch file that walks the tree with FOR /R and calls accoreconsole once per DWG with the same script. Each drawing gets its own console process, so a failure or a crash affects one file rather than the whole run, and per-file output is easy to log. This is what most office 'batch purge', 'batch plot to PDF' and 'batch title-block update' tools reduce to once the LISP or .NET part is written.
tools.usage:
for /R "<root folder>" %%F in (*.dwg) do <accoreconsole> /i "%%F" /s "<script.scr>" /isolate

; %%F inside a .bat file, %F when typed directly at the command prompt

parameters.name: FOR /R
parameters.description: Recurses the whole tree below the root folder. FOR %%F IN (folder\*.dwg) without /R stays in one folder.

parameters.name: %%F quoting
parameters.description: Always wrap "%%F" in quotes - project paths contain spaces - and use %%F in a .bat file but %F when typing the same loop at a prompt.

parameters.name: /isolate
parameters.description: Keeps each drawing's system-variable changes inside its own console process so nothing leaks into the interactive product or into the next file.

parameters.name: logging
parameters.description: Redirect stdout and stderr per file (> "log\%%~nF.log" 2>&1) so a failed drawing can be identified afterwards; %%~nF is the file name without path or extension.

parameters.name: exclusions
parameters.description: Skip backups and recovery copies (*.bak, *.sv$) and check for a .dwl/.dwl2 lock file next to the DWG, which means someone has the drawing open and the console will not be able to save it.

parameters.name: copy first
parameters.description: Scripts that save in place are destructive. Copy the tree, or have the script SAVEAS into an output folder, before running anything across live project data.

parameters.name: parallelism
parameters.description: Several console processes can run at once (start /b, or a PowerShell ForEach-Object -Parallel), limited by cores and by the licence terms of the installation.

tools.notes: PowerShell gives the same loop with better error handling: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Filter *.dwg | ForEach-Object { & $acc /i $_.FullName /s $scr /isolate }. If the script must receive per-drawing parameters, write them to a JSON or CSV file that a .NET command loaded with NETLOAD reads - scripts themselves cannot take arguments.

tools.name: FILEDIA / ATTDIA
tools.description: The two system variables that decide whether a scripted command stops to show a dialog. FILEDIA 0 turns every file-selection dialog into a command-line prompt, so OPEN, SAVEAS, -WBLOCK, SCRIPT, NETLOAD and LINETYPE ask for a path as text; ATTDIA 0 makes INSERT prompt for attribute values on the command line instead of opening the Edit Attributes dialog. Setting both to 0 at the top of any script is a rule, not a suggestion: a dialog that appears during playback consumes the script's remaining lines as keystrokes and corrupts the drawing.
tools.usage:
FILEDIA
0
ATTDIA
0
ATTREQ
1

; restore at the end
FILEDIA
1
ATTDIA
1

parameters.name: FILEDIA
parameters.description: 1 (default) shows file dialogs; 0 prompts for file names on the command line. Typing a tilde (~) at such a prompt forces the dialog to appear anyway, which is handy interactively.

parameters.name: ATTDIA
parameters.description: 0 (default in a clean profile) prompts for block attribute values on the command line; 1 opens the Edit Attributes dialog. Scripts that run -INSERT on attributed blocks must have it at 0.

parameters.name: ATTREQ
parameters.description: 1 prompts for attribute values on insertion; 0 uses the defaults silently, which is what a script wants when it will set the values afterwards with ATTSYNC, -ATTEDIT or code.

parameters.name: EXPERT
parameters.description: Suppresses 'are you sure' prompts (overwrite existing file, redefine block, purge confirmation). Values 0-5 progressively silence more of them; set it back to 0 afterwards because a high EXPERT hides real mistakes.

parameters.name: CMDECHO
parameters.description: 0 stops the command line echoing every prompt, which makes a script's log readable; it is a LISP-level setting normally restored to 1.

parameters.name: restore
parameters.description: These are profile-stored, not drawing-stored, so an interactive session left with FILEDIA 0 confuses the next user. Restore them at the end of the script, or run under accoreconsole /isolate so the change cannot escape.

tools.example:
; insert an attributed title block from a script without a single dialog
FILEDIA
0
ATTDIA
0
ATTREQ
1
_-INSERT
TB_A1=C:/standards/blocks/TB_A1.dwg
0,0
1
1
0
P-1042
A-101
REV C
2026-09-19
_QSAVE
FILEDIA
1
ATTDIA
1
tools.notes: Other dialog switches worth knowing in the same context: PICKADD and PICKFIRST affect how selections behave inside macros, and LAYERDLGMODE / -LAYER decide whether layer work opens the palette. Under accoreconsole no dialog can display at all, but commands still branch on FILEDIA, so set it to 0 there too.

tools.name: APPLOAD
tools.description: Load an application into the current session: AutoLISP source or compiled code (.lsp, .fas, .vlx), a VBA project (.dvb), an ObjectARX module (.arx, .dbx, .crx) or a managed .NET assembly (.dll). The dialog also holds the Startup Suite, a per-profile list of applications that are loaded automatically into every drawing, which is how most offices deploy their LISP library without editing acaddoc.lsp. Loading is subject to SECURELOAD and TRUSTEDPATHS, so files outside a trusted folder raise a security prompt or are refused outright.
tools.usage:
APPLOAD  (alias AP)
(dialog) Load / Unload / Contents (Startup Suite) / Add to History

; equivalents that work in a script or from code
(load "C:/lisp/tools.lsp")
(arxload "C:/arx/tools.arx")
NETLOAD  C:\bundles\Tools.dll

parameters.name: Load
parameters.description: Load the selected file into the current session. LISP loaded this way lives only in the current drawing document unless it is in the Startup Suite.

parameters.name: Unload
parameters.description: Available for ObjectARX and VBA modules only. AutoLISP definitions and .NET assemblies cannot be unloaded - the session has to be restarted.

parameters.name: Startup Suite (Contents)
parameters.description: Per-profile list of files loaded into every drawing that is opened. Stored in the registry with the profile, so exporting the profile with an .arg file carries it to another machine.

parameters.name: Add to History
parameters.description: Keeps loaded files in the History list for quick reloading during development.

parameters.name: file types
parameters.description: .lsp, .fas, .vlx, .dvb, .arx, .dbx, .crx, .dll. The dialog filters by type; a .NET assembly can also be loaded with NETLOAD.

parameters.name: security
parameters.description: SECURELOAD decides whether files outside TRUSTEDPATHS may load at all; the Startup Suite is not exempt.

tools.example:
; Interactive
APPLOAD
(browse to C:\lisp\office.vlx, Load)
(Contents > Add > C:\lisp\office.vlx  - loads in every drawing from now on)

; Script-safe alternative - no dialog involved
FILEDIA
0
(load "C:/lisp/office.vlx")

; From .NET, load another assembly at run time
; ExtensionLoader.Load(@"C:\bundles\Tools.dll");
tools.notes: There is no -APPLOAD. In scripts use (load ...) for LISP, NETLOAD for .NET and (arxload ...) or ARX Load for ObjectARX. Deploying through the Autodesk App Store bundle format (a .bundle folder with PackageContents.xml under ApplicationPlugins) is the modern alternative: it loads automatically, needs no Startup Suite entry and is what Design Automation AppBundles use.

tools.name: NETLOAD
tools.description: Load a managed .NET assembly into the AutoCAD process so the [CommandMethod] and [LispFunction] members it defines become available as commands and LISP functions. The assembly is loaded in-process, which is why .NET code is far faster than out-of-process COM for bulk editing, and why it is the API that accoreconsole and Design Automation support. It respects FILEDIA, so a script can load an assembly by typing the path at the prompt.
tools.usage:
NETLOAD
Select .NET Assembly dialog

; script form
FILEDIA
0
NETLOAD
C:\bundles\Tools.dll

parameters.name: assembly path
parameters.description: Full path to the .dll. Dependencies are resolved from the same folder or from the probing path, so ship referenced assemblies alongside it.

parameters.name: FILEDIA
parameters.description: 0 turns the file dialog into a command-line prompt - the only way NETLOAD can be used inside a .scr script or a Core Console run.

parameters.name: no unload
parameters.description: A loaded assembly cannot be unloaded; the file stays locked until AutoCAD exits. During development this is handled by loading from a copy, or by a debug build that shadow-copies.

parameters.name: version match
parameters.description: The assembly must be built against the acmgd/acdbmgd/accoremgd of a compatible release and the right .NET runtime (.NET Framework 4.8 for AutoCAD 2021-2024, .NET 8 for AutoCAD 2025 and later). Copy Local should be false for the AutoCAD references.

parameters.name: SECURELOAD
parameters.description: Applies to .NET as well: an assembly outside a trusted path prompts, or is blocked when SECURELOAD is 2.

parameters.name: IExtensionApplication
parameters.description: If the assembly implements it, Initialize() runs at load time and Terminate() at shutdown - the place to register overrules, reactors or ribbon content.

tools.example:
; batch script that loads an add-in and runs one of its commands
FILEDIA
0
SECURELOAD
0
NETLOAD
C:\bundles\TitleBlockTool.dll
UPDATETITLEBLOCK
C:\batch\params.json
_QSAVE

; run headless
accoreconsole.exe /i "D:\1042\A-101.dwg" /s "C:\batch\update.scr" /isolate
tools.notes: Lowering SECURELOAD inside a script is a real security decision; the cleaner route is to add the bundle folder to TRUSTEDPATHS in the batch profile. AutoCAD 2025 moved to .NET 8, so assemblies built for earlier releases must be retargeted; keep separate builds per release family.

tools.name: ARX
tools.description: Manage native ObjectARX applications from the command line: list what is loaded, load and unload modules, list the commands and classes a module registered, and set the options that control how ARX modules are demand-loaded. Unlike .NET assemblies, ARX modules can genuinely be unloaded, which makes this command useful during development and when a module has to be replaced without restarting AutoCAD.
tools.usage:
ARX
Enter an option [?/Load/Unload/Commands/Options]: ?

; AutoLISP equivalents
(arxload "C:/arx/tools.arx")
(arxunload "tools")
(arx)        ; list loaded modules

parameters.name: ? (list)
parameters.description: List the ObjectARX modules currently loaded in the session.

parameters.name: Load
parameters.description: Load an .arx, .dbx or .crx module. With FILEDIA 0 the path is typed at the command line, which is what a script needs.

parameters.name: Unload
parameters.description: Unload a module by name. Modules that registered custom object classes or that are locked by open custom objects refuse to unload.

parameters.name: Commands
parameters.description: List the command groups and the global and local command names each loaded module registered with acedRegCmds.

parameters.name: Options
parameters.description: Controls demand loading behaviour - whether a module is loaded on detection of its custom objects, on invocation of one of its commands, or at startup.

parameters.name: acad.rx
parameters.description: The startup list of ARX modules; anything named there loads automatically when AutoCAD starts.

tools.example:
; load, inspect and unload during development
ARX
L
C:\dev\MyTool\x64\Release\MyTool.arx

ARX
C            ; which commands did it register?

ARX
U
MyTool

; from LISP
(if (not (member "mytool.arx" (arx))) (arxload "C:/dev/MyTool/MyTool.arx"))
tools.notes: ObjectARX binaries are tied to an AutoCAD release family and must be rebuilt for each one; loading a mismatched module fails with a version error rather than crashing. Demand loading is configured per module in the registry by its installer, which is what makes a custom object open correctly in a drawing sent to another machine.

tools.name: VLIDE
tools.description: Open the Visual LISP integrated development environment: an editor with syntax colouring for AutoLISP, a console for evaluating expressions against the live drawing, a debugger with breakpoints, step and watch windows, an inspector for objects and selection sets, and a Make Application wizard that compiles .lsp sources into a .fas module or a packaged .vlx application. It is the traditional home of serious LISP development and the place where (vl-load-com) ActiveX code is most easily tested.
tools.usage:
VLIDE   (also VLISP)

; typical session
File > New / Open       - edit .lsp
Tools > Load Text in Editor (Ctrl+Alt+E)
Console window: (c:MYCOMMAND)  or  (vlax-dump-object obj T)
Debug > Toggle Breakpoint (F9), Step Into (F8)
File > Make Application > New Application Wizard  - build .fas / .vlx

parameters.name: Console window
parameters.description: Evaluates AutoLISP expressions immediately against the current drawing, the fastest way to test (ssget) filters, entget lists and vla-* calls.

parameters.name: Load Text in Editor
parameters.description: Loads the whole file, or just the selection, into the running session without saving to disk first.

parameters.name: Debugger
parameters.description: Breakpoints, step in/over/out, Watch and Inspect windows, and the Trace stack - LISP's only real debugging facility.

parameters.name: Make Application wizard
parameters.description: Compiles sources into a .fas (compiled LISP) or .vlx (application package that can bundle several files and a DCL), optionally with the source protected.

parameters.name: Inspect
parameters.description: Opens an object browser on an entity name, VLA object or selection set, showing every property and method available through ActiveX.

parameters.name: vlax-dump-object
parameters.description: Console helper that prints all properties and, with T as the second argument, all methods of a VLA object - the practical substitute for reading the COM type library.

tools.example:
; In the VLIDE console, explore the COM object model live
(vl-load-com)
(setq acad (vlax-get-acad-object))
(setq doc  (vla-get-ActiveDocument acad))
(vlax-dump-object doc T)

(setq ms (vla-get-ModelSpace doc))
(vla-AddCircle ms (vlax-3d-point 0 0 0) 25.0)
(vla-ZoomExtents acad)
tools.notes: VLIDE is Windows-only and is now the legacy editor: Autodesk also ships an AutoLISP extension for Visual Studio Code with syntax checking, debugging against a running AutoCAD and project support, which is the recommended environment for new work. Compiled .fas/.vlx files still have to be produced by the Make Application wizard.

tools.name: acad.lsp / acaddoc.lsp / acad.rx
tools.description: The three files AutoCAD looks for on the support file search path at startup so that custom code loads without anyone pressing a button. acad.lsp is loaded once per session (or once per drawing if ACADLSPASDOC is 1), acaddoc.lsp is loaded into every drawing document as it opens, and acad.rx lists ObjectARX modules to load at startup. A function named S::STARTUP defined in any of them runs after the drawing is fully initialised, which is the only safe place to issue commands or set drawing-level system variables.
tools.usage:
; search order: the first file of each name found on the support path wins
acad.lsp      -> once per session (per document if ACADLSPASDOC = 1)
acaddoc.lsp   -> once per drawing document, after acad.lsp
acad.rx       -> plain list of .arx modules, one per line
<name>.mnl    -> loaded with the matching <name>.cuix

(defun S::STARTUP () ... )   ; runs after the drawing is initialised

parameters.name: acad.lsp
parameters.description: Session-level LISP. Good for defining functions and loading libraries; not the place for (command ...) calls, because no drawing is ready yet.

parameters.name: acaddoc.lsp
parameters.description: Document-level LISP, loaded for every drawing including new ones. The usual home for an office standard library: (load "office.vlx").

parameters.name: acad.rx
parameters.description: Text file listing ObjectARX modules to load at startup, one path or module name per line.

parameters.name: S::STARTUP
parameters.description: Reserved function name called after the drawing is open and initialised - the correct place to run commands, set CLAYER or insert a block automatically.

parameters.name: ACADLSPASDOC
parameters.description: 0 (default) loads acad.lsp once per session; 1 loads it into every document. Affects only acad.lsp, never acaddoc.lsp.

parameters.name: acad<release>.lsp / acad<release>doc.lsp
parameters.description: Autodesk's own startup files (acad2025.lsp, acad2025doc.lsp). They are reserved for the product and must not be edited; put custom code in acad.lsp or acaddoc.lsp instead.

parameters.name: .mnl
parameters.description: A LISP file loaded automatically with the .cuix of the same name, so menu and ribbon macros can call functions that are guaranteed to be loaded.

tools.example:
; acaddoc.lsp on the office support path
(vl-load-com)
(if (findfile "office.vlx") (load "office.vlx"))

(defun S::STARTUP ()
  (setvar "FILEDIA" 1)
  (setvar "ATTDIA" 0)
  (setvar "INSUNITS" 4)          ; millimetres
  (if (not (tblsearch "LAYER" "DEFPOINTS"))
      (command "_.-LAYER" "_M" "DEFPOINTS" ""))
  (princ))

; acad.rx
C:\bundles\MyCustomObjects.dbx
tools.notes: Only one S::STARTUP can exist; a second definition silently replaces the first, so libraries that need startup work should append to it rather than redefine it. These files are loaded only if they are found on the support file search path (OPTIONS > Files), and they are subject to SECURELOAD like any other executable file. The .bundle/PackageContents.xml mechanism under ApplicationPlugins is the modern, per-release-aware alternative.

tools.name: SECURELOAD / TRUSTEDPATHS
tools.description: The security gate that decides whether AutoCAD will run executable code - LISP, ARX, .NET, VBA - from a given folder. SECURELOAD sets the policy and TRUSTEDPATHS lists the folders whose contents are trusted; files in the AutoCAD installation folder are always trusted. Batch and deployment work has to account for these, because a perfectly good script that calls NETLOAD or (load ...) from a network share will otherwise stop on a security prompt that no unattended process can answer.
tools.usage:
SECURELOAD
Enter new value for SECURELOAD <1>: 0 | 1 | 2

TRUSTEDPATHS
Enter new value for TRUSTEDPATHS: C:\standards\lisp;C:\bundles\...

; a trailing \... includes subfolders of that path

parameters.name: SECURELOAD 0
parameters.description: Load and execute files from anywhere without asking. Convenient, and exactly the behaviour the setting exists to prevent; acceptable only on an isolated batch machine.

parameters.name: SECURELOAD 1
parameters.description: Default. Files outside a trusted path raise a warning dialog that the user must accept before the file loads.

parameters.name: SECURELOAD 2
parameters.description: Files outside a trusted path are refused outright with no prompt - the setting for a locked-down environment.

parameters.name: TRUSTEDPATHS
parameters.description: Semicolon-separated list of folders. A path on its own trusts only the files directly in it; ending the entry with \... also trusts every subfolder.

parameters.name: TRUSTEDDOMAINS
parameters.description: Companion variable listing domains from which files may be loaded or downloaded by web-enabled features.

parameters.name: install folder
parameters.description: The AutoCAD program folder and its ApplicationPlugins bundles are trusted implicitly and do not need to be listed.

parameters.name: profile scope
parameters.description: Both variables are stored with the user profile, not the drawing, so a batch profile (acad.exe /p or accoreconsole /isolate) can carry its own relaxed setting without changing the user's.

tools.example:
; office deployment: trust the standards tree once, then load normally
TRUSTEDPATHS
C:\standards\lisp;\\server\cad\bundles\...
SECURELOAD
1

; from AutoLISP, add a folder without wiping the existing list
(setvar "TRUSTEDPATHS"
        (strcat (getvar "TRUSTEDPATHS") ";C:\\bundles\\..."))

; from .NET
; Application.SetSystemVariable("SECURELOAD", 0);
tools.notes: A UNC path can be trusted, but AutoCAD warns that a network folder is only as safe as its write permissions. If unattended jobs keep stopping, check TRUSTEDPATHS before reaching for SECURELOAD 0: relaxing the policy globally is the change that gets blamed after an incident.

tools.name: AutoCAD.Application
tools.description: The COM entry point. AutoCAD registers the ProgID AutoCAD.Application, so any COM-capable language can create or attach to a session and get back an AcadApplication object whose ActiveDocument and Documents collection lead to everything else. The connection is out-of-process: every property read and method call is a cross-process marshalled call, which is fine for a few hundred operations and painfully slow for tens of thousands - use the in-process .NET API for bulk edits. This is also the only API Python, VBScript and Excel VBA can reach.
tools.usage:
; ProgID
"AutoCAD.Application"            ; latest installed release
"AutoCAD.Application.25"         ; a specific release's ProgID

; VBA / VBScript
Set acad = GetObject(, "AutoCAD.Application")   ' attach to a running session
Set acad = CreateObject("AutoCAD.Application")  ' start one if needed
acad.Visible = True
Set doc = acad.ActiveDocument

parameters.name: Visible
parameters.description: Shows or hides the AutoCAD window. A session started by COM is invisible until this is set True; an invisible session still needs a licence and can still be left running by a crashed script.

parameters.name: ActiveDocument
parameters.description: The AcadDocument for the drawing currently in focus; also settable, which is how code switches between open drawings.

parameters.name: Documents
parameters.description: Collection of open drawings. Documents.Add([template]) creates one, Documents.Open(path, [readOnly]) opens one, Item(i) and Count enumerate, and Close() closes them all.

parameters.name: Document.SaveAs / Save / Close
parameters.description: doc.SaveAs(path[, fileType]) writes the drawing, doc.Save() saves in place and doc.Close([SaveChanges][, FileName]) closes it - the three calls every COM batch loop ends with.

parameters.name: Document.Regen
parameters.description: doc.Regen(acAllViewports) rebuilds the display after code has changed geometry; entity-level Update() refreshes a single object.

parameters.name: ZoomExtents / ZoomAll / ZoomWindow
parameters.description: Zoom methods live on the Application object, not the document: acad.ZoomExtents() after creating geometry, otherwise the new objects may be off screen.

parameters.name: Quit
parameters.description: Closes the session. Without it an invisible automation instance survives the calling script and holds the drawing file open.

parameters.name: Preferences
parameters.description: AcadPreferences object exposing the Options dialog settings (Files, Display, OpenSave, Output, System, UserPreferences, Drafting, Selection, Profiles).

tools.example:
' Excel VBA: open every drawing listed in column A, purge and save
Dim acad As Object, doc As Object, i As Long
On Error Resume Next
Set acad = GetObject(, "AutoCAD.Application")
If acad Is Nothing Then Set acad = CreateObject("AutoCAD.Application")
On Error GoTo 0
acad.Visible = True

For i = 2 To Cells(Rows.Count, 1).End(xlUp).Row
    Set doc = acad.Documents.Open(Cells(i, 1).Value)
    doc.PurgeAll
    doc.SetVariable "CLAYER", "0"
    acad.ZoomExtents
    doc.Save
    doc.Close
Next i

acad.Quit
tools.notes: GetObject with no first argument attaches to a running instance and raises an error if none exists; the try-attach-then-create pattern above is standard. A COM client sees only one AutoCAD instance per user session in practice, so COM does not parallelise - for throughput run several accoreconsole processes instead. If the user is mid-command, COM calls fail or queue: check doc.GetVariable("CMDACTIVE") before driving a live session.

tools.name: AcadDocument.ModelSpace / PaperSpace / Layouts
tools.description: The three containers that hold drawable objects in a COM session. ModelSpace is the block that holds full-scale geometry, PaperSpace is the block belonging to the currently active layout, and the Layouts collection gives access to every sheet in the drawing with its plot configuration. Because PaperSpace always refers to the active layout, code that touches several sheets sets ActiveLayout first, then works through PaperSpace or through the Layout's own Block property.
tools.usage:
Set ms = doc.ModelSpace              ' AcadModelSpace  (block *Model_Space)
Set ps = doc.PaperSpace              ' AcadPaperSpace of the ACTIVE layout
doc.ActiveSpace = acModelSpace       ' acModelSpace = 1, acPaperSpace = 0

Set lay = doc.Layouts.Add("A-102")
doc.ActiveLayout = doc.Layouts.Item("A-102")
Set blk = doc.Layouts.Item("A-102").Block   ' that sheet's geometry
n = ms.Count : Set ent = ms.Item(0)

parameters.name: ModelSpace
parameters.description: Collection of every entity in model space, with Count and Item(i) for enumeration and the Add* factory methods for creation.

parameters.name: PaperSpace
parameters.description: The active layout's paper-space block. Switching ActiveLayout changes what PaperSpace points at, so cache entity references, not the container.

parameters.name: ActiveSpace
parameters.description: Switches the drawing between model and paper space (the TILEMODE/viewport state). Setting it fails if the drawing has no layout.

parameters.name: Layouts
parameters.description: Collection of AcadLayout objects. Add(name), Item(name or index), Count; each layout has Name, TabOrder, Block and a full set of plot properties.

parameters.name: Layout plot properties
parameters.description: ConfigName (the .pc3 or printer), CanonicalMediaName (paper size), PlotType, StandardScale, UseStandardScale, PlotRotation, CenterPlot, StyleSheet (.ctb/.stb), PlotWithLineweights.

parameters.name: RefreshPlotDeviceInfo
parameters.description: Must be called on a Layout or PlotConfiguration after changing ConfigName, before the media names and scales of the new device are valid.

parameters.name: doc.Plot
parameters.description: The AcadPlot object: SetLayoutsToPlot(array of names), NumberOfCopies, QuietErrorMode, PlotToDevice([config]) and PlotToFile(file[, config]) for scripted output.

parameters.name: MSpace
parameters.description: doc.MSpace = True enters floating model space inside the active viewport of a layout; False returns to paper space.

tools.example:
' Create a sheet, put a viewport on it and plot it to PDF
Set lay = doc.Layouts.Add("A-102")
doc.ActiveLayout = lay
lay.ConfigName = "DWG To PDF.pc3"
lay.RefreshPlotDeviceInfo
lay.CanonicalMediaName = "ISO_full_bleed_A1_(841.00_x_594.00_MM)"
lay.StyleSheet = "monochrome.ctb"
lay.PlotWithLineweights = True

Dim c(0 To 2) As Double
c(0) = 420#: c(1) = 297#: c(2) = 0#
Set vp = doc.PaperSpace.AddPViewport(c, 700#, 450#)
vp.Display True
vp.CustomScale = 0.01                     ' 1:100

doc.Plot.QuietErrorMode = True
doc.Plot.PlotToFile "C:\out\A-102.pdf"
tools.notes: AddPViewport only works while the layout is active and returns a viewport that is off until Display True is called. Layout names are case-insensitive and must be unique; deleting the last layout is not allowed. Plotting through COM depends on the device being installed for the interactive user, which is one of the reasons plot automation is often left in a script run by acad.exe /b rather than the Core Console.

tools.name: AcadDocument.Blocks / AcadDocument.Layers
tools.description: The two symbol-table collections that most automation touches. Blocks holds every block definition in the drawing, including the special *Model_Space and *Paper_Space blocks and any xref definitions, and a new AcadBlock is filled with the same Add* factory methods used on model space. Layers holds AcadLayer objects with colour, linetype, lineweight, plot style, on/off, freeze, lock and plottable state, and doc.ActiveLayer sets the current layer that new geometry inherits.
tools.usage:
Set blk = doc.Blocks.Add(originPoint, "VALVE_GATE")   ' new definition
blk.AddLine p1, p2                                    ' fill it
Set ref = doc.ModelSpace.InsertBlock(pt, "VALVE_GATE", 1#, 1#, 1#, 0#)

Set lay = doc.Layers.Add("WALLS")
lay.color = acRed
lay.Lineweight = acLnWt050
doc.ActiveLayer = lay

parameters.name: Blocks.Add(basePoint, name)
parameters.description: Creates an empty block definition whose origin is the given point; entities added to the returned AcadBlock become its content.

parameters.name: Blocks.Item / Count / Delete
parameters.description: Look up or enumerate definitions. IsXRef, IsLayout, Path and Units on an AcadBlock tell you what kind of definition you are looking at.

parameters.name: Layers.Add(name)
parameters.description: Creates or returns the layer. Layer names may not contain < > / \ " : ; ? * | , = ` and are limited to 255 characters.

parameters.name: AcadLayer properties
parameters.description: color (an AcadAcCmColor or an ACI index), Linetype, Lineweight, PlotStyleName, LayerOn, Freeze, Lock, Plottable, Description, ViewportDefault.

parameters.name: Linetypes.Load
parameters.description: doc.Linetypes.Load "HIDDEN", "acad.lin" must run before a layer can be given that linetype, otherwise assignment fails.

parameters.name: ActiveLayer
parameters.description: The layer new entities are created on. Entities also expose their own Layer property, which is usually set explicitly rather than relying on the current layer.

parameters.name: Delete restrictions
parameters.description: Layer 0, DEFPOINTS in use, the current layer, xref-dependent layers and any layer with objects on it cannot be deleted; PurgeAll removes the unused ones.

parameters.name: Attributes
parameters.description: A block definition holds AcadAttribute objects created with blk.AddAttribute(height, mode, prompt, insertionPoint, tag, value); the inserted reference exposes them through GetAttributes().

tools.example:
' Build a tagged symbol definition once, then place it many times
Dim o(0 To 2) As Double: o(0) = 0#: o(1) = 0#: o(2) = 0#
Set blk = doc.Blocks.Add(o, "EQUIP_TAG")
Dim c(0 To 2) As Double: c(0) = 0#: c(1) = 0#: c(2) = 0#
blk.AddCircle c, 5#
blk.AddAttribute 2.5, acAttributeModeVerify, "Tag number:", c, "TAG_NO", "P-000"

Dim p(0 To 2) As Double
For i = 1 To 5
    p(0) = i * 200#: p(1) = 0#: p(2) = 0#
    Set ref = doc.ModelSpace.InsertBlock(p, "EQUIP_TAG", 1#, 1#, 1#, 0#)
    atts = ref.GetAttributes
    atts(0).TextString = "P-10" & i
    ref.Update
Next i
tools.notes: Redefining an existing block through COM means deleting the definition's entities and re-adding them; every reference updates immediately. Layer and block changes are not undone by the user's UNDO in the tidy way interactive edits are, because COM work is not grouped - wrap batches with doc.StartUndoMark / doc.EndUndoMark so a user can step back out of them in one go.

tools.name: AcadDocument.SelectionSets
tools.description: COM's way of gathering existing objects. A named AcadSelectionSet is created on the document, filled by Select (programmatic modes such as all, window, crossing, last), SelectOnScreen (the user picks), SelectAtPoint or AddItems, and then enumerated with Count and Item. Filtering uses the same DXF group codes as AutoLISP's ssget: code 0 for entity type, 8 for layer, 2 for block name, 6 for linetype, 62 for colour, with -4 introducing logical operators.
tools.usage:
Set ss = doc.SelectionSets.Add("SS1")
ss.Select acSelectionSetAll, , , FilterType, FilterData
ss.SelectOnScreen FilterType, FilterData
ss.AddItems objectArray
For Each ent In ss : ... : Next
ss.Delete

parameters.name: SelectionSets.Add(name)
parameters.description: Creates the set. Adding a name that already exists raises an error, so the standard idiom is to try Item(name), Delete it, then Add.

parameters.name: Select(mode, [pt1], [pt2], [filterType], [filterData])
parameters.description: Modes include acSelectionSetAll, acSelectionSetWindow, acSelectionSetCrossing, acSelectionSetPrevious, acSelectionSetLast and the polygon and fence variants; window and crossing need the two corner points.

parameters.name: SelectOnScreen
parameters.description: Prompts the user to pick objects, honouring the same filter. Requires an interactive session - it cannot be used from the Core Console or a service.

parameters.name: AddItems / RemoveItems / Clear
parameters.description: Add or remove an array of objects you already hold references to; Clear empties the set without deleting it.

parameters.name: filterType / filterData
parameters.description: Parallel arrays: an Integer array of DXF group codes and a Variant array of the matching values. Both must be passed ByRef as real arrays, not literals.

parameters.name: -4 operators
parameters.description: "<AND", "AND>", "<OR", "OR>", "<NOT", "NOT>" and comparison operators like "<=" paired with code -4, exactly as in ssget filters, allow compound conditions.

parameters.name: Erase / Highlight / Update
parameters.description: Set-level operations: Erase deletes every member, Highlight True flashes them, Update redraws them after property changes.

parameters.name: Delete
parameters.description: Removes the named set from the document. Leaving sets behind wastes drawing resources and eventually collides with the next Add of the same name.

tools.example:
' Every TEXT and MTEXT on layer NOTES, moved to layer ANNO
Dim ft(0 To 2) As Integer
Dim fd(0 To 2) As Variant
ft(0) = -4: fd(0) = "<OR"
ft(1) = 0:  fd(1) = "TEXT,MTEXT"
ft(2) = -4: fd(2) = "OR>"

On Error Resume Next
doc.SelectionSets.Item("SS1").Delete
On Error GoTo 0
Set ss = doc.SelectionSets.Add("SS1")
ss.Select acSelectionSetAll, , , ft, fd

For Each ent In ss
    If ent.Layer = "NOTES" Then ent.Layer = "ANNO"
Next ent
Debug.Print ss.Count & " objects retagged"
ss.Delete
tools.notes: A single filter entry can carry a comma-separated list ("TEXT,MTEXT") without any operator, which is simpler than an <OR block when only the entity type varies. Wildcards work in name filters ("A-*" for layers). Selection sets live in the drawing and survive until deleted, so long-running COM clients should always clean up. In .NET the equivalent is Editor.SelectAll / GetSelection with a SelectionFilter of TypedValues.

tools.name: AcadDocument.Utility
tools.description: The COM object that handles user input and value conversion. Its Get* methods put a prompt on the AutoCAD command line and block until the user answers, returning points, distances, angles, strings, integers, reals, keywords or a picked entity; its conversion methods translate between the internal representation and formatted strings using the drawing's UNITS settings. It is the only part of the COM model that needs a human, so it is also the part that must never appear in headless code.
tools.usage:
pt  = doc.Utility.GetPoint([basePoint], "\nPick a point: ")
dist = doc.Utility.GetDistance(pt, "\nLength: ")
ang = doc.Utility.GetAngle(pt, "\nAngle: ")            ' returns radians
doc.Utility.GetEntity ent, pickPt, "\nSelect an object: "   ' ByRef out params
s = doc.Utility.AngleToString(ang, acDegreeMinuteSeconds, 4)
doc.Utility.Prompt "\n12 objects processed."

parameters.name: GetPoint / GetCorner / GetDistance / GetAngle
parameters.description: Point and measurement input, optionally rubber-banded from a base point. Angles come back in radians regardless of the drawing's angular units.

parameters.name: GetEntity(object, pickedPoint, prompt)
parameters.description: Asks the user to pick one object and returns both the object and the pick point through ByRef parameters - which is why it reads as a tuple in Python and as two output variables in VBA.

parameters.name: GetString / GetInteger / GetReal / GetKeyword
parameters.description: Text and numeric input. GetString's first argument decides whether spaces end the input (False) or are allowed (True).

parameters.name: InitializeUserInput(bits, keywords)
parameters.description: Applied before a Get* call: bit 1 disallows null input, 2 disallows zero, 4 disallows negatives, 32 draws a dashed rubber band; the keyword string supplies the options the user may type instead of a value.

parameters.name: AngleToString / AngleToReal / DistanceToReal / RealToString
parameters.description: Convert between internal doubles and formatted text using unit constants such as acDegrees, acDegreeMinuteSeconds, acGrads, acRadians - the right way to build text that matches the drawing's units.

parameters.name: TranslateCoordinates
parameters.description: Converts a point between WCS, UCS, OCS/ECS and DCS - essential when an entity's coordinates are reported in its own object coordinate system.

parameters.name: Prompt
parameters.description: Writes a message to the command line, the COM equivalent of Editor.WriteMessage. Start the string with a newline so it does not append to the current prompt.

parameters.name: PolarPoint / CreateTypedArray
parameters.description: PolarPoint(basePoint, angle, distance) computes a point; CreateTypedArray builds the typed VARIANT arrays that filter and coordinate parameters expect.

tools.example:
' Label the length of a line the user picks
Dim ent As Object, pickPt As Variant
doc.Utility.GetEntity ent, pickPt, vbCrLf & "Select a line: "

If TypeName(ent) = "IAcadLine" Then
    Dim mid(0 To 2) As Double
    mid(0) = (ent.StartPoint(0) + ent.EndPoint(0)) / 2
    mid(1) = (ent.StartPoint(1) + ent.EndPoint(1)) / 2
    mid(2) = 0#
    Set t = doc.ModelSpace.AddText(Format(ent.Length, "0.0"), mid, 2.5)
    t.Layer = "ANNO"
    doc.Utility.Prompt vbCrLf & "Length " & Format(ent.Length, "0.0") & " labelled."
End If
tools.notes: Every Get* call raises a COM error when the user presses Esc, so wrap them in error handling rather than letting the client crash. Input requires the AutoCAD window to be the active application; an invisible automation instance will simply hang. For batch work take parameters from a file or the command line instead, and in .NET use Editor.GetPoint/GetSelection with PromptStatus checks.

tools.name: AcadModelSpace.AddLine / AddCircle / AddText / InsertBlock
tools.description: The factory methods that create geometry through COM. Every drawable container - ModelSpace, PaperSpace and any AcadBlock - exposes the same family: AddLine, AddCircle, AddArc, AddEllipse, AddLightWeightPolyline, AddPolyline, AddSpline, AddPoint, AddRegion, AddHatch, AddText, AddMText, AddAttribute, the AddDim* dimension methods, AddLeader, AddTable and InsertBlock. Each returns the new object, whose Layer, Color, Linetype, LinetypeScale and TrueColor are then set as properties; there is no equivalent of the command line's option prompts.
tools.usage:
Set ln  = ms.AddLine(startPt, endPt)
Set ci  = ms.AddCircle(centrePt, radius)
Set ar  = ms.AddArc(centrePt, radius, startAngleRad, endAngleRad)
Set pl  = ms.AddLightWeightPolyline(verticesArray)      ' flat array of X,Y pairs
Set tx  = ms.AddText("PLATE 12mm", insertPt, height)
Set mt  = ms.AddMText(insertPt, width, "1. Notes...")
Set dim = ms.AddDimAligned(extLine1Pt, extLine2Pt, textPt)
Set br  = ms.InsertBlock(insertPt, "VALVE_GATE", 1#, 1#, 1#, rotationRad)

parameters.name: point arguments
parameters.description: Every point is a VARIANT array of three doubles in WCS - a Double(0 To 2) in VBA, array.array('d', [x, y, z]) with pywin32, APoint(x, y) with pyautocad. Passing a plain tuple or list usually fails with a type mismatch.

parameters.name: angles in radians
parameters.description: AddArc, InsertBlock's rotation and every angle property take radians, not degrees. Converting with Atn(1) * 4 / 180 is the commonest source of wrong-looking output.

parameters.name: AddLightWeightPolyline
parameters.description: Takes a flat array of 2D coordinates (x1, y1, x2, y2, ...) at the current elevation; set Closed = True afterwards and use SetWidth / SetBulge per segment for width and arcs.

parameters.name: AddText vs AddMText
parameters.description: AddText(string, insertionPoint, height) creates a single-line TEXT; AddMText(insertionPoint, width, string) creates an MTEXT that word-wraps at the given width and accepts inline formatting codes such as \\P for a new paragraph.

parameters.name: AddDimAligned / AddDimRotated / AddDimRadial / AddDimAngular
parameters.description: Dimension factories; the created dimension picks up the current dimension style, which is set beforehand through doc.ActiveDimStyle.

parameters.name: InsertBlock(point, name, xs, ys, zs, rot[, password])
parameters.description: The Name argument may be a block already defined in the drawing or a full path to an external .dwg, in which case the file is imported as a new definition. Negative scales mirror the reference.

parameters.name: AddHatch(patternType, patternName, associativity)
parameters.description: Creates an empty hatch (acHatchPatternTypePredefined and a name such as "ANSI31"); boundaries are then supplied with AppendOuterLoop and AppendInnerLoop, each taking an array of objects, and the hatch is finished with Evaluate and Update.

parameters.name: Update / Delete
parameters.description: Every returned object has Update() to refresh its display after property changes and Delete() to erase it. Nothing is visible until the display regenerates.

tools.example:
' A dimensioned plate outline built entirely through COM
Dim p(0 To 7) As Double
p(0) = 0#:   p(1) = 0#
p(2) = 200#: p(3) = 0#
p(4) = 200#: p(5) = 120#
p(6) = 0#:   p(7) = 120#
Set pl = doc.ModelSpace.AddLightWeightPolyline(p)
pl.Closed = True
pl.Layer = "OUTLINE"

Dim c(0 To 2) As Double: c(0) = 50#: c(1) = 60#: c(2) = 0#
Set hole = doc.ModelSpace.AddCircle(c, 8#)
hole.Layer = "OUTLINE"

Dim a(0 To 2) As Double, b(0 To 2) As Double, t(0 To 2) As Double
a(0) = 0#: a(1) = 0#: a(2) = 0#
b(0) = 200#: b(1) = 0#: b(2) = 0#
t(0) = 100#: t(1) = -25#: t(2) = 0#
Set d = doc.ModelSpace.AddDimAligned(a, b, t)
d.Layer = "DIMS"

acad.ZoomExtents
tools.notes: There is no Add* method for every command: chamfers, fillets, trims, arrays and most editing operations have no COM equivalent and are reached either through SendCommand or by computing the result geometrically and creating it directly. Bulk creation through COM is slow because each call crosses the process boundary; for thousands of objects use .NET inside a single transaction.

tools.name: AcadDocument.SendCommand
tools.description: The escape hatch: send a string to the command line exactly as if it had been typed, which reaches every command including the hundreds with no COM equivalent. The string must end with a space or a carriage return to be executed, embedded spaces and \n act as Enter, and the usual _ and - prefixes apply. In recent releases the text is queued rather than executed synchronously, so a SendCommand call may still be pending when the next line of client code runs - never interleave it with direct object-model calls that depend on its result.

parameters.name: trailing space or vbCr
parameters.description: Without it the command text sits at the prompt unexecuted. This is the single most common SendCommand bug.

parameters.name: _ and - prefixes
parameters.description: Use _ for language independence and - for the command-line version of dialog commands, exactly as in a script: "_.-INSERT ".

parameters.name: leading period
parameters.description: "_.LINE" runs the built-in command even if an alias or LISP redefinition has taken the name.

parameters.name: asynchronous queueing
parameters.description: The call returns before the command finishes in current releases. Code that must act on the result should do the whole job in one sent string, or in LISP called by that string, rather than in the client.

parameters.name: FILEDIA / ATTDIA
parameters.description: Anything sent that would open a dialog blocks the queue with no way to answer it, so set both to 0 first, exactly as in a script.

parameters.name: (command ...) payloads
parameters.description: A sent string may be a whole LISP expression, which is the usual way to get conditional logic, loops and error handling into an operation that COM must trigger.

parameters.name: .NET SendStringToExecute
parameters.description: The managed equivalent, with flags for activating the document, wrapping up an inactive document and echoing the command; it is likewise deferred until the current command ends.

parameters.name: CMDACTIVE
parameters.description: System variable to check before sending, so the call does not arrive in the middle of a command the user is running.

tools.example:
' Plot the current layout to PDF - a job with no clean COM equivalent
doc.SetVariable "FILEDIA", 0
doc.SetVariable "BACKGROUNDPLOT", 0

doc.SendCommand "_.-PLOT _Y " & _
                "" & vbCr & _
                "DWG To PDF.pc3" & vbCr & _
                "ISO full bleed A1 (841.00 x 594.00 MM)" & vbCr & _
                "_M _L _N _E _F _C _Y monochrome.ctb _Y _N _N _Y " & _
                "C:\out\sheet.pdf" & vbCr & "_N _Y "

doc.SetVariable "FILEDIA", 1
tools.notes: BACKGROUNDPLOT 0 matters whenever plotting is driven from code: with background plotting on, the client can close the drawing before the plot spools. Because the queue is per-document, sending to a document that is not active silently defers the text until it becomes active - activate it first with acad.ActiveDocument = doc.

tools.name: AcadDocument.GetVariable / AcadDocument.SetVariable
tools.description: Read and write AutoCAD system variables from COM. Between them these two calls reach several hundred settings that have no other object-model representation - FILEDIA, ATTDIA, INSUNITS, CLAYER, DIMSCALE, PDMODE, OSMODE, TEXTSIZE, LTSCALE, TILEMODE - and they are how scripted work configures the environment before it starts. Values come back as VARIANTs whose type matches the variable: a string, an integer, a double, or an array of doubles for point variables.
tools.usage:
v = doc.GetVariable("CLAYER")            ' -> "WALLS"
doc.SetVariable "CLAYER", "ANNO"
doc.SetVariable "FILEDIA", 0
ins = doc.GetVariable("INSBASE")         ' -> array of 3 doubles

; other APIs
; LISP:  (getvar "CLAYER")  (setvar "CLAYER" "ANNO")
; .NET:  Application.GetSystemVariable("CLAYER");
;        Application.SetSystemVariable("CLAYER", "ANNO");

parameters.name: variable name
parameters.description: Case-insensitive. SETVAR ? at the command line lists every variable and its current value, which is the quickest way to find the one that controls a behaviour.

parameters.name: return type
parameters.description: String, Integer, Double or a 2/3-element array of Doubles. Assigning a point variable requires a properly typed array, not a list.

parameters.name: read-only variables
parameters.description: Many variables (DWGNAME, DWGPREFIX, ACADVER, LOGINNAME, CDATE) cannot be set; attempting it raises a COM error.

parameters.name: storage scope
parameters.description: Some variables are saved in the drawing, some in the user profile (registry) and some only for the session. Profile-stored changes made in a batch leak into the interactive product unless the work runs under accoreconsole /isolate or a separate acad.exe /p profile.

parameters.name: restore pattern
parameters.description: Read the old value, set the new one, do the work, put the old one back - standard practice for OSMODE, FILEDIA, CMDECHO and DIMSCALE.

parameters.name: drawing properties
parameters.description: Variables like DWGNAME and DWGPREFIX identify the current file; doc.FullName and doc.Path give the same information as real properties.

parameters.name: SETVAR command
parameters.description: The command-line equivalent, usable from a script or through SendCommand when a variable must be changed as part of a queued command sequence.

tools.example:
' Configure a drawing for scripted work, then restore the user's settings
Dim oldFiledia, oldOsmode, oldCmdecho
oldFiledia = doc.GetVariable("FILEDIA")
oldOsmode = doc.GetVariable("OSMODE")
oldCmdecho = doc.GetVariable("CMDECHO")

doc.SetVariable "FILEDIA", 0
doc.SetVariable "OSMODE", 0          ' no object snaps hijacking coordinates
doc.SetVariable "CMDECHO", 0
doc.SetVariable "INSUNITS", 4        ' millimetres
doc.SetVariable "CLAYER", "0"

' ... create geometry ...

doc.SetVariable "FILEDIA", oldFiledia
doc.SetVariable "OSMODE", oldOsmode
doc.SetVariable "CMDECHO", oldCmdecho
tools.notes: Setting OSMODE to 0 before generating geometry from code is almost always right: with running snaps on, points sent to commands get pulled onto nearby objects. Variables that are stored in the drawing (LTSCALE, DIMSCALE, INSUNITS, PSLTSCALE) must be set per document, not once per session.

tools.name: pyautocad / win32com.client
tools.description: Python has no native AutoCAD API; it reaches AutoCAD over the same COM interface as VBA, either directly with pywin32 (win32com.client) or through pyautocad, a thin wrapper built on comtypes that adds the helpers the raw interface lacks. The main friction is data types: every point must be a VARIANT array of doubles, and the named constants VBA gets for free have to be imported or spelled out numerically. Everything else mirrors the COM model exactly, so VBA examples translate almost line for line.
tools.usage:
# pywin32, late binding
import win32com.client, array
acad = win32com.client.Dispatch("AutoCAD.Application")

# pywin32, early binding: generates a type library wrapper and gives constants
acad = win32com.client.gencache.EnsureDispatch("AutoCAD.Application")
from win32com.client import constants

# pyautocad
from pyautocad import Autocad, APoint, aDouble
acad = Autocad(create_if_not_exists=True)

parameters.name: Dispatch vs GetActiveObject
parameters.description: Dispatch starts AutoCAD if it is not running; win32com.client.GetActiveObject("AutoCAD.Application") attaches only to a running session and raises com_error otherwise.

parameters.name: point arrays
parameters.description: With pywin32 use array.array('d', [x, y, z]); with pyautocad use APoint(x, y[, z]) and aDouble(*values) for vertex lists. A plain Python list or tuple raises a type mismatch.

parameters.name: EnsureDispatch
parameters.description: Early binding through makepy: gives IntelliSense-style attributes, correct types for ByRef output parameters and the win32com.client.constants namespace for acSelectionSetAll and friends.

parameters.name: acad.model / acad.doc
parameters.description: pyautocad shortcuts for ActiveDocument.ModelSpace and ActiveDocument; acad.iter_objects("Text") and acad.iter_objects_fast() iterate model space with an optional type filter.

parameters.name: ByRef output parameters
parameters.description: Methods like Utility.GetEntity return their outputs as a tuple in Python (entity, pick_point = doc.Utility.GetEntity()) rather than filling variables passed in.

parameters.name: com_error handling
parameters.description: Every COM failure surfaces as pywin32's com_error / comtypes' COMError; wrap calls in try/except, particularly around Utility input, which raises when the user presses Esc.

parameters.name: performance
parameters.description: Each attribute access is a cross-process call. Cache doc, model space and frequently used objects in local names, and prefer one SendCommand for bulk editing operations over thousands of property writes.

parameters.name: maintenance status
parameters.description: pyautocad is a small, long-unmaintained convenience layer; pywin32 with early binding is the more durable choice for new work and gives access to the whole type library.

tools.example:
import array
import win32com.client

def pt(x, y, z=0.0):
    return array.array('d', [x, y, z])

acad = win32com.client.Dispatch("AutoCAD.Application")
acad.Visible = True
doc = acad.ActiveDocument
ms = doc.ModelSpace

doc.SetVariable("OSMODE", 0)
doc.SetVariable("CLAYER", "0")

# a bolt circle: 8 holes on a 120 mm pitch circle
import math
for i in range(8):
    a = 2 * math.pi * i / 8
    ms.AddCircle(pt(60 * math.cos(a), 60 * math.sin(a)), 5.0)

outer = ms.AddCircle(pt(0, 0), 80.0)
outer.Layer = "OUTLINE"

txt = ms.AddText("8 x M10 EQUALLY SPACED", pt(-70, -100), 6.0)
txt.Layer = "ANNO"

acad.ZoomExtents()
doc.SaveAs(r"C:\out\flange.dwg")
tools.notes: Python drives AutoCAD out of process only - there is no in-process Python API, so no Python equivalent of NETLOAD, no Python in accoreconsole and none in Design Automation. Where Python is needed in a headless pipeline, the usual split is Python for orchestration (walking folders, calling accoreconsole, parsing the JSON a .NET command wrote) and .NET for the work inside the drawing.

tools.name: Application.DocumentManager.MdiActiveDocument
tools.description: The starting point of almost every managed .NET routine: the Document object for the drawing that is currently active, from which the Database and the Editor are reached. DocumentManager also opens, adds and enumerates documents, and supplies the document lock that code running in application context must take before it may modify a drawing. In accoreconsole and Design Automation there is exactly one document and MdiActiveDocument is it.

parameters.name: MdiActiveDocument
parameters.description: The active drawing. Null in rare application-context situations with no open document, so check before dereferencing in event handlers.

parameters.name: DocumentManager.Open / Add
parameters.description: Open(path, forReadOnly) opens a drawing in the editor and Add(template) creates one. Both need CommandFlags.Session on the calling command, because documents cannot be opened from document context.

parameters.name: LockDocument()
parameters.description: Returns a DocumentLock that must be held (in a using block) whenever a drawing is modified from application context - a modeless palette, an event handler, a background thread or a Session command.

parameters.name: Core.Application
parameters.description: Autodesk.AutoCAD.ApplicationServices.Core.Application in accoremgd.dll exposes DocumentManager and system-variable access without pulling in the GUI-bound acmgd.dll, which is what makes an assembly runnable in the Core Console and in Design Automation.

parameters.name: doc.Name / doc.Database.Filename
parameters.description: Full path of the drawing; the way a batch command discovers which file it is working on when parameters come from a folder walk.

parameters.name: Document events
parameters.description: DocumentCreated, DocumentActivated, DocumentToBeDestroyed and CommandWillStart/CommandEnded on the document itself, for add-ins that react to what the user does.

parameters.name: CommandFlags.Session
parameters.description: Marks a [CommandMethod] as running in application context, which is required for opening, closing or switching documents from code.

tools.notes: Opening drawings through DocumentManager loads them into the editor, which is slow and needs the full product; when only the data matters, open a side Database with ReadDwgFile instead and never create a Document at all. In the Core Console, DocumentManager exists but has a single document and no MDI, so code that iterates documents must not assume more than one.

tools.name: Database
tools.description: The DWG itself as an object: all the symbol tables, the named object dictionary, every entity, and the drawing-level settings. Code normally works on the active drawing's database (doc.Database), but it can also open a DWG file directly into a side database with ReadDwgFile and save it with SaveAs, without ever opening it in the editor - by far the fastest way to process large numbers of drawings, and the technique behind most batch tools.

parameters.name: new Database(buildDefaultDrawing, noDocument)
parameters.description: new Database(false, true) creates an empty database with no default content, ready to receive a DWG with ReadDwgFile; new Database(true, true) builds one from the default template settings.

parameters.name: ReadDwgFile / SaveAs / CloseInput
parameters.description: Read a DWG into the database, write it back out at a chosen DwgVersion, and release the file handle. Always dispose the side database, normally with a using block.

parameters.name: symbol table ids
parameters.description: BlockTableId, LayerTableId, TextStyleTableId, DimStyleTableId, LinetypeTableId, ViewportTableId, UcsTableId and NamedObjectsDictionaryId - the entry points a transaction opens.

parameters.name: drawing settings
parameters.description: Clayer, Tilemode, Insunits, Ltscale, Dimscale, Pdmode, Extmin/Extmax and dozens more are properties of the Database rather than system variables when working on a side database.

parameters.name: WorkingDatabase
parameters.description: HostApplicationServices.WorkingDatabase is what unqualified API calls act on; set it to a side database for code (including some ObjectARX-derived calls) that assumes a current drawing, and restore it afterwards.

parameters.name: WblockCloneObjects
parameters.description: Copies objects between databases with their dependencies (layers, styles, block definitions) resolved, using an IdMapping and a DuplicateRecordCloning rule - the supported way to import content from another DWG.

parameters.name: ResolveXrefs / xref handling
parameters.description: A side database does not load xrefs unless asked; ResolveXrefs binds or loads them when the batch needs the referenced geometry.

parameters.name: SummaryInfo
parameters.description: DatabaseSummaryInfo and DatabaseSummaryInfoBuilder read and write the drawing properties (title, subject, author, custom fields) that title-block fields bind to.

tools.notes: A side database has no Editor, so nothing in that code path may prompt, write to the command line or depend on the current view. Saving with DwgVersion.Current keeps the installed release's format; pass an explicit version such as DwgVersion.AC1032 when downstream consumers need an older one. Objects from one database may never be added to another directly - clone them.

tools.name: TransactionManager.StartTransaction
tools.description: The unit of work in the .NET API. Every read or write of a database object goes through a transaction: StartTransaction returns a Transaction, GetObject opens objects for read or write inside it, new objects are registered with AddNewlyCreatedDBObject, and Commit makes the whole set of changes permanent and closes every object that was opened. If Commit is not called - because of an exception, an early return or a forgotten line - the transaction aborts on disposal and every change is silently discarded.

parameters.name: GetObject(id, OpenMode)
parameters.description: Opens a DBObject by ObjectId, ForRead or ForWrite. An object already open for read in the same transaction is upgraded with UpgradeOpen() rather than opened again.

parameters.name: AddNewlyCreatedDBObject(obj, true)
parameters.description: Tells the transaction about an object just appended to a container so it is committed and disposed correctly. Forgetting it leaves the object orphaned or crashes on commit.

parameters.name: Commit / Abort
parameters.description: Commit writes the changes; Abort (or simply disposing without Commit) rolls them all back. Both close the objects the transaction opened.

parameters.name: using block
parameters.description: Always wrap the transaction in using so it is disposed on an exception path. Do not dispose objects obtained from GetObject - the transaction owns them.

parameters.name: nested transactions
parameters.description: Transactions may be nested; an inner Abort undoes only its own work. TransactionManager.TopTransaction gives the outermost one, and NumberOfActiveTransactions reports the depth.

parameters.name: OpenCloseTransaction
parameters.description: A lighter alternative (db.TransactionManager.StartOpenCloseTransaction()) with less bookkeeping, useful for simple read-only passes over many objects.

parameters.name: document lock
parameters.description: When the code runs in application context, take doc.LockDocument() before starting the transaction, or the write fails with eLockViolation.

parameters.name: one transaction per batch
parameters.description: Opening and committing a transaction per object is the classic performance mistake; one transaction around a whole batch of edits is dramatically faster and gives the user a single undo step.

tools.notes: An exception thrown inside the using block skips Commit, so a partially completed edit is rolled back cleanly - this is a feature, not a problem, and is why catch blocks should not call Commit. Erased objects are opened with GetObject(id, OpenMode.ForWrite, true) when the third argument allows erased objects. Graphics do not refresh until the transaction commits and the editor regenerates.

tools.name: BlockTable / BlockTableRecord
tools.description: The symbol table that holds every block definition in a database, plus the two special records that are model space and paper space. Reaching geometry in .NET always goes through it: open the BlockTable from db.BlockTableId, index it with BlockTableRecord.ModelSpace to get the model space record, and append entities there. The same record type is used for real block definitions, so creating a block means creating a BlockTableRecord, adding it to the table and appending entities to it.

parameters.name: BlockTableRecord.ModelSpace / PaperSpace
parameters.description: Constants for the reserved names "*Model_Space" and "*Paper_Space". Use them rather than the literal strings, and remember paper space here means the record for the current layout.

parameters.name: AppendEntity(entity)
parameters.description: Adds an entity to the record and returns its new ObjectId. It must be followed by tr.AddNewlyCreatedDBObject(entity, true) in the same transaction.

parameters.name: bt.Has(name) / bt[name]
parameters.description: Test for a block definition and get its ObjectId. Indexing a name that does not exist throws, so test first when the name comes from user data.

parameters.name: bt.Add(record)
parameters.description: Adds a new BlockTableRecord (a block definition) to the table; the BlockTable must be open for write, which is usually done with UpgradeOpen().

parameters.name: GetBlockReferenceIds(directOnly, forceValidity)
parameters.description: Returns every BlockReference that points at this definition - the way to count insertions or to update all of them after a redefinition.

parameters.name: Origin / Units / Explodable
parameters.description: Properties of a block definition: its base point, insertion units for automatic scaling, and whether insertions may be exploded.

parameters.name: IsLayout / IsFromExternalReference
parameters.description: Flags distinguishing layout records and xref definitions from ordinary blocks when iterating the whole table.

parameters.name: AttributeDefinition
