parameters.description: Attribute definitions are entities appended to the block's record; the matching AttributeReference objects are appended to each BlockReference with AppendAttribute.

tools.notes: Entities must be fully constructed before being appended; setting properties that depend on the database (Layer, Linetype, annotative scale) only works after the object is database-resident. Model space in a side database is reached exactly the same way, which is why the same helper code serves both interactive and headless batch work.

tools.name: Editor
tools.description: The .NET interface to the command line and the pointing device for a given document: prompts for points, distances, angles, keywords, strings and entities, builds selection sets with or without a filter, writes messages, and controls the view and the current selection. Every prompt returns a Prompt*Result whose Status must be checked against PromptStatus.OK before its Value is used, because the user may cancel or press Enter. None of it exists in a side database, and in the Core Console there is no user to answer.

parameters.name: WriteMessage
parameters.description: Writes to the command line, with a leading \n so the text starts on its own line. Supports composite format strings. In the Core Console this is what lands in stdout and therefore in the batch log.

parameters.name: GetPoint / GetDistance / GetAngle / GetCorner
parameters.description: Geometric input. PromptPointOptions adds a base point for rubber-banding, keywords, and flags such as AllowNone and UseBasePoint.

parameters.name: GetSelection / SelectAll / SelectCrossingWindow
parameters.description: Selection. GetSelection prompts the user; SelectAll and the SelectWindow/SelectCrossingWindow/SelectFence family select programmatically without any prompt, which is what batch code uses.

parameters.name: SelectionFilter / TypedValue
parameters.description: new SelectionFilter(new[] { new TypedValue((int)DxfCode.Start, "LINE"), new TypedValue((int)DxfCode.LayerName, "WALLS") }) - the same DXF group codes as ssget and COM filters.

parameters.name: PromptStatus
parameters.description: OK, Cancel, None, Keyword, Error. Checking it is mandatory; using .Value after a cancel throws or returns garbage.

parameters.name: GetString / GetInteger / GetDouble / GetKeywords
parameters.description: Text and numeric input, with PromptStringOptions.AllowSpaces and keyword lists configured through the matching *Options objects.

parameters.name: Regen / UpdateScreen / SetImpliedSelection
parameters.description: View and selection housekeeping after a batch of edits: regenerate the drawing, flush graphics, or leave the objects the command created selected.

parameters.name: Command / CommandAsync
parameters.description: ed.Command(...) runs an AutoCAD command with its arguments from .NET (AutoCAD 2015 and later), the managed counterpart of acedCommandS - safer than SendStringToExecute because it executes in order.

tools.notes: A dynamic block reference reports an anonymous name (*U12) in br.Name; read DynamicBlockTableRecord for the real one, as above. Code that must run both interactively and headless should take its parameters from a file or command arguments and use SelectAll rather than GetSelection, so the same assembly works under accoreconsole.

tools.name: [CommandMethod]
tools.description: The attribute that turns a public method in a loaded .NET assembly into an AutoCAD command. AutoCAD scans every assembly loaded with NETLOAD for it, so no registration code is needed: mark the method, load the DLL, type the name. Overloads add a command group, separate global and localised names, and CommandFlags that control where and how the command may run - the most important being Session, which puts the command in application context so it may open and close documents.

parameters.name: global name
parameters.description: The command name typed at the prompt. It must not clash with a built-in command; a prefix of two or three letters identifying the add-in is the usual convention.

parameters.name: command group
parameters.description: A namespace for commands so two add-ins can define the same name; the group is what CUI macros and the ARX Commands listing report.

parameters.name: CommandFlags.Modal / Transparent
parameters.description: Modal (the default) means the command cannot run while another command is active; Transparent allows it to run inside another command, which severely restricts what it may do.

parameters.name: CommandFlags.Session
parameters.description: Runs in application context rather than document context - required to open, create, close or switch documents, and to drive several drawings in one command.

parameters.name: CommandFlags.UsePickSet / Redraw
parameters.description: UsePickSet lets the command consume objects the user selected before starting it (via ed.SelectImplied); Redraw keeps that selection highlighted.

parameters.name: CommandFlags.NoPaperSpace / NoTileMode / NoBlockEditor
parameters.description: Refuse to run in contexts the command cannot handle, producing AutoCAD's standard message instead of a crash.

parameters.name: method signature
parameters.description: Public, non-static or static, and parameterless. The declaring class must be public and must have a public parameterless constructor; one instance is created per document.

parameters.name: IExtensionApplication
parameters.description: Implement it on one class in the assembly to run Initialize() at load and Terminate() at shutdown - where ribbon content, overrules and event handlers are registered.

tools.notes: A command that must run in the Core Console has to avoid the Editor's interactive prompts and anything in acmgd.dll that touches the GUI; reference accoremgd.dll and Autodesk.AutoCAD.ApplicationServices.Core.Application instead. Commands are also how Design Automation activities invoke a bundle: the activity's script simply types the command name.

tools.name: [LispFunction]
tools.description: The attribute that exposes a .NET method to AutoLISP as a callable function, so existing LISP code can hand work to compiled code without being rewritten. The method receives a ResultBuffer holding the arguments as TypedValues and returns a ResultBuffer (or null for nil), with LispDataType codes describing each value. It is the standard bridge in offices with a large LISP investment: the LISP keeps the workflow and the .NET does the heavy lifting or the work LISP cannot do.

parameters.name: function name
parameters.description: The name LISP will call. Hyphens and a vendor prefix are conventional (of-sum, acme:extract) and avoid clashes with built-in functions.

parameters.name: ResultBuffer args
parameters.description: The arguments as TypedValues in call order; null when the function was called with none. Iterate with args.AsArray().

parameters.name: LispDataType codes
parameters.description: Text, Int16, Int32, Double, Point2d, Point3d, ObjectId, SelectionSetName, ListBegin, ListEnd, DottedPair, Nil, T_atom - both for reading arguments and for building the return value.

parameters.name: return value
parameters.description: A ResultBuffer describing one value or a list (wrapped in ListBegin/ListEnd markers); returning null gives nil in LISP.

parameters.name: entity names
parameters.description: LISP entity names arrive as LispDataType.ObjectId, so a function can take an (entsel) result directly and open it in a transaction.

parameters.name: selection sets
parameters.description: A selection set passed from (ssget) arrives as LispDataType.SelectionSetName, which .NET resolves through the Editor's SelectionSet handling.

parameters.name: document context
parameters.description: The function runs in the calling document's context, so the active document's database is the right one to work on - no document lock is needed.

parameters.name: error reporting
parameters.description: Throwing an exception surfaces in LISP as an application error; returning nil and writing a message with Editor.WriteMessage is usually friendlier to existing LISP callers.

tools.notes: [LispFunction] methods are found by the same assembly scan as [CommandMethod], so NETLOAD is all that is needed to publish them. Values cross the boundary by copy, so returning a huge list is expensive; return an ObjectId or write a file when the payload is large. LISP itself is not available in Design Automation, so a bundle should expose commands rather than LISP functions.

tools.name: DBObject open / append / Commit pattern
tools.description: The five-step shape that almost every managed AutoCAD routine takes, worth treating as a single idiom: get the document and database, start a transaction, open the container (usually model space) through the BlockTable, create or open and modify the objects, then commit. Objects are never opened directly - only through a transaction, by ObjectId - and they are never disposed by the caller, because the transaction closes them. Modifying an object opened for read requires UpgradeOpen, and deleting means Erase, not a .NET delete.

parameters.name: ObjectId vs Handle
parameters.description: ObjectId is valid only for the session and database it came from; Handle is persistent and stored in the DWG. Store Handles between sessions and convert with db.GetObjectId(false, handle, 0).

parameters.name: OpenMode.ForRead / ForWrite
parameters.description: Open for read by default and upgrade only when a change is actually needed - it is cheaper and avoids write-lock conflicts with other code.

parameters.name: UpgradeOpen / DowngradeOpen
parameters.description: Switch an already-open object between read and write inside the same transaction. Opening the same object twice for write in one transaction throws.

parameters.name: Erase()
parameters.description: Marks an object erased (recoverable by undo) rather than removing it. Iterating a container afterwards still returns erased ids unless they are filtered with IsErased.

parameters.name: Dispose rules
parameters.description: Objects returned by GetObject belong to the transaction - do not dispose them. Objects created with new and never appended to a database must be disposed (a using block) or they leak.

parameters.name: database residency
parameters.description: Properties that depend on the drawing (Layer, Linetype, annotative scales, extension dictionaries) can only be set after the entity has been appended and registered.

parameters.name: extension dictionary / XData
parameters.description: Custom data hangs off any DBObject: CreateExtensionDictionary plus an Xrecord for structured data, or RegAppTable plus XData for the older group-code style that LISP can also read.

parameters.name: DocumentLock
parameters.description: Required whenever the edit originates outside a document-context command - palettes, events, Session commands, background work. Not needed inside an ordinary [CommandMethod].

tools.notes: The layer must exist before it is assigned or the assignment throws eKeyNotFound - create missing layers in the same transaction. Erasing while iterating a BlockTableRecord is safe because the iterator works over ids, not live objects. For very large batches, Database.SaveAs after the transaction is cheaper than leaving the drawing open in the editor.

tools.name: acrxEntryPoint / acedRegCmds
tools.description: The two pieces every ObjectARX module is built around. acrxEntryPoint is the exported C++ function AutoCAD calls with load, unload, load-drawing and unload-drawing messages, and it is where the module locks or unlocks itself, declares MDI awareness and registers or removes its commands. acedRegCmds is the global command stack: addCommand publishes a command with a group name, a global (English) name, a localised name, flags and a function pointer, and removeGroup withdraws the whole set at unload.

parameters.name: kInitAppMsg / kUnloadAppMsg
parameters.description: Sent when the module is loaded and unloaded. Register commands, custom classes and reactors in the first, and remove all of them in the second.

parameters.name: kLoadDwgMsg / kUnloadDwgMsg
parameters.description: Sent per document in an MDI session; the place for per-drawing initialisation once registerAppMDIAware has been called.

parameters.name: unlockApplication / registerAppMDIAware
parameters.description: unlockApplication(pkt) permits the module to be unloaded with ARX Unload; registerAppMDIAware(pkt) declares that it copes with multiple open documents.

parameters.name: addCommand(group, global, local, flags, fn)
parameters.description: Registers one command. The global name is the English one scripts and macros should use; flags are ACRX_CMD_MODAL, ACRX_CMD_TRANSPARENT, ACRX_CMD_USEPICKSET, ACRX_CMD_SESSION and so on.

parameters.name: removeGroup(group)
parameters.description: Removes every command registered under that group; failing to do this at unload leaves dangling function pointers and crashes the next invocation.

parameters.name: ACRX_DXF_DEFINE_MEMBERS
parameters.description: The macro pair (ACRX_DECLARE_MEMBERS in the header) that gives a custom AcDbObject class its runtime class information, needed for any custom entity or object.

parameters.name: ACED_ARXCOMMAND_ENTRY_AUTO
parameters.description: The macro used by the ObjectARX wizard's AcRxArxApp framework to register a command automatically, removing the hand-written addCommand calls.

parameters.name: module types
parameters.description: .arx for a normal application, .dbx for a module that only defines custom objects (so it can be loaded by any DWG host), .crx for a Core Console compatible module.

tools.notes: ObjectARX binaries are bound to a release family and must be rebuilt (and re-signed for the App Store) for each one; a mismatched module is refused at load with a version message. Because ARX code runs in the AutoCAD process with no sandbox, an access violation takes the whole session down - which is the practical reason most new work is done in .NET unless custom objects, reactors, overrules or raw speed demand C++.

tools.name: acedCommand / acedGetPoint
tools.description: The ADS-style C functions that let ObjectARX code talk to the command processor and the user exactly as AutoLISP does. acedCommand sends a command with its arguments as a variable-length list of type/value pairs terminated by RTNONE, and the acedGet* family puts prompts on the command line and returns RTNORM, RTCAN or RTNONE according to what the user did. They are the quickest route to functionality that has no direct database equivalent, at the cost of going through the command layer.

parameters.name: acedCommand / acedCommandS / acedCmdS
parameters.description: Send a command. acedCommand is the historical form; newer SDKs provide the synchronous acedCommandS and acedCmdS, which execute in order and are the ones to use now that command execution can otherwise be deferred.

parameters.name: result type codes
parameters.description: RTSTR, RTREAL, RTSHORT, RTLONG, RTPOINT, RT3DPOINT, RTENAME, RTPICKS, RTNONE - each value in the argument list is preceded by its type code and the list ends with RTNONE.

parameters.name: acedGetPoint(base, prompt, result)
parameters.description: Point input with optional rubber-band base point. Returns RTNORM on success, RTCAN if the user cancelled, RTNONE if they pressed Enter.

parameters.name: acedGetString / acedGetReal / acedGetInt / acedGetKword
parameters.description: The rest of the input family; acedGetString's first argument controls whether spaces terminate the input.

parameters.name: acedInitGet(bits, keywords)
parameters.description: Applied before a Get call to disallow null, zero or negative input and to define the keywords the user may type instead of a value - identical in meaning to LISP's (initget).

parameters.name: acedSSGet
parameters.description: Builds a selection set with the same mode strings and DXF filter lists as LISP's (ssget), returning an ads_name that acedSSLength and acedSSName then walk.

parameters.name: acutPrintf
parameters.description: Writes formatted text to the command line - the ObjectARX equivalent of Editor.WriteMessage.

parameters.name: acedGetVar / acedSetVar
parameters.description: Read and write system variables from C++, using a resbuf to carry the typed value.

tools.notes: Going through the command processor means the user's running object snaps, current layer and command echo all apply, so set OSMODE and CLAYER deliberately first - the same discipline scripts need. For bulk geometry creation, building AcDbEntity objects and appending them to the block table record is both faster and immune to those side effects.

tools.name: AcDbLine / AcDbBlockTableRecord
tools.description: The native C++ database classes, the layer that the .NET and COM models are wrappers over. Entities such as AcDbLine, AcDbCircle, AcDbArc, AcDbPolyline, AcDbText, AcDbMText and AcDbBlockReference derive from AcDbEntity; containers such as AcDbBlockTableRecord and the other symbol tables derive from AcDbObject. Creating geometry means constructing the entity on the heap, opening model space for write, appending it and closing everything - C++ has no transaction by default, so open/close discipline is manual and unforgiving.

parameters.name: workingDatabase()
parameters.description: acdbHostApplicationServices()->workingDatabase() is the database unqualified calls act on; a module that processes side databases sets and restores it explicitly.

parameters.name: ACDB_MODEL_SPACE / ACDB_PAPER_SPACE
parameters.description: The reserved block names, used with AcDbBlockTable::getAt to obtain the record that holds model or paper space geometry.

parameters.name: appendAcDbEntity(id, entity)
parameters.description: Adds the entity to the record and returns its AcDbObjectId. After this the database owns the entity: call close(), never delete.

parameters.name: close()
parameters.description: Every object opened or appended must be closed, and closing must happen in reverse order of opening. A missed close leaves the object locked for the rest of the session.

parameters.name: acdbOpenObject / acdbOpenAcDbEntity
parameters.description: Open an existing object by id for read or write - the C++ counterpart of Transaction.GetObject; the smart-pointer templates AcDbObjectPointer<T> close automatically and are the modern form.

parameters.name: entity properties
parameters.description: setLayer(), setColorIndex(), setLinetype(), setLinetypeScale(), setTransparency() work only once the entity is database-resident, exactly as in .NET.

parameters.name: AcDbBlockReference
parameters.description: Insert a block by constructing it from a point and the definition's AcDbObjectId, then appending attribute references with appendAttribute().

parameters.name: AcDbBlockTableRecordIterator
parameters.description: Walks the entities in a record (newIterator / start / done / step / getEntity), the C++ way to iterate model space.

tools.notes: The ownership rule is absolute: an entity that was appended belongs to the database and must be closed, while one that was never appended must be deleted. Getting it wrong is the classic ObjectARX memory bug. AcDbDatabase also supports transactions through acdbHostApplicationServices()->workingDatabase()->transactionManager(), which behaves like the .NET transaction and is worth using in complex code.

tools.name: ^C^C command macro
tools.description: The macro string behind every ribbon button, toolbar icon, menu item, shortcut key and tool palette tool, written in the CUI editor's Macro field. A macro is script syntax with a few extra control characters: ^C^C to cancel whatever is running, a backslash to pause for user input, a semicolon for Enter, and the same _ and - prefixes scripts use. Unlike a script it can pause for the user mid-way, which is what makes macros the right tool for small, repeatable, semi-interactive jobs that do not justify writing code.
tools.usage:
^C^C_-LAYER;_M;DIM;;_RECTANG;\@100,50

; character meanings
^C^C   cancel twice (leaves any nested command)
_      force the English command name
-      command-line version of a dialog command
.      the built-in command, ignoring aliases and redefinitions
;      Enter   (a trailing space is also Enter)
\      pause for one user input
*      leading * repeats the macro until Esc: *^C^C_MOVE
^Z     trailing ^Z suppresses the automatic Enter at the end of the macro
$M=    introduces a DIESEL expression

parameters.name: ^C^C
parameters.description: Two cancels, because one only backs out of the current option level. Standard at the start of almost every macro so the button works no matter what the user was doing.

parameters.name: \ (backslash)
parameters.description: Pauses the macro for exactly one user input - a point, a distance, a selection or a keyword. Selection of multiple objects needs the command's own Enter to end it.

parameters.name: ; (semicolon)
parameters.description: An Enter keystroke. Two semicolons give two Enters, which is how a macro accepts a default and then ends a command.

parameters.name: * prefix
parameters.description: Placed before ^C^C it repeats the whole macro until the user presses Esc - the behaviour of the built-in repeating tools.

parameters.name: ^Z suffix
parameters.description: Suppresses the Enter that AutoCAD otherwise appends to the end of a macro, needed when the last command must stay waiting for input.

parameters.name: $M= DIESEL
parameters.description: Evaluates a DIESEL string expression at run time, for example $M=$(if,$(=,$(getvar,cvport),1),_MSPACE,_PSPACE) to make one button do the right thing in each space.

parameters.name: (LISP calls)
parameters.description: A macro may call any loaded AutoLISP function - ^C^C(c:myroutine) - which is how branching and error handling get into a button; the matching .mnl file guarantees the function is loaded.

parameters.name: CUI / CUILOAD
parameters.description: Macros live in a .cuix edited with the CUI command; CUILOAD and CUIUNLOAD attach and detach partial customization files, so office macros can ship separately from the main menu.

tools.example:
; Button 1 - set a layer, then draw a 100x50 rectangle at a point the user picks
^C^C_-LAYER;_M;DIM;;_RECTANG;\@100,50

; Button 2 - repeating trim with all objects as the cutting edge
*^C^C_.TRIM;;

; Button 3 - plot the current layout to PDF with no dialogs
^C^C_FILEDIA;0;_-PLOT;_Y;;DWG To PDF.pc3;;_M;_L;_N;_E;_F;_C;_Y;monochrome.ctb;_Y;_N;_N;_Y;_FILEDIA;1;

; Button 4 - call a LISP routine loaded by the matching .mnl
^C^C(if (not c:ofgrid) (load "office.vlx"));(c:ofgrid)

; Button 5 - zoom to the extents of the active space, whichever it is
^C^C$M=$(if,$(=,$(getvar,tilemode),1),_.ZOOM _E,_.ZOOM _E)
tools.notes: Spaces inside a macro are Enters, so a file name or a text string containing spaces must be quoted or entered through a pause. Test macros by typing the same sequence at the command line first: if it works there with every option spelled out, it will work as a macro. Because macros are stored per .cuix, keeping office macros in a partial customization file avoids losing them when the main menu is upgraded.

tools.name: ACTRECORD / ACTSTOP / ACTPLAY / ACTMANAGER
tools.description: The Action Recorder: a no-code macro recorder that captures command input as an .actm action macro and replays it on demand. ACTRECORD starts recording, every command and response is logged, and ACTSTOP ends the recording and prompts for a name and description. ACTPLAY replays a macro, ACTMANAGER lists and edits the saved ones, and ACTUSERINPUT marks a step where playback should pause for the user to supply a value - the only interactivity an action macro has.
tools.usage:
ACTRECORD                 ; start recording (red dot on the status bar)
  ... run commands ...
ACTUSERINPUT              ; insert a pause-for-user step while recording
ACTBASEPOINT              ; record a base point so the macro is relocatable
ACTSTOP                   ; stop and save as <name>.actm

ACTPLAY  <name>           ; play it back
ACTMANAGER                ; manage, rename, copy, delete, edit values

parameters.name: ACTRECORD
parameters.description: Begins recording all command input in the current drawing. Panel and palette actions, dialog interactions and grip edits record poorly or not at all - stay on the command line.

parameters.name: ACTSTOP
parameters.description: Ends recording and opens the Action Macro dialog for the name, command alias, description and playback options.

parameters.name: ACTPLAY
parameters.description: Replays a saved macro by name. Because a macro is also given a command alias, typing the macro's name at the prompt runs it directly.

parameters.name: ACTUSERINPUT
parameters.description: Inserts a Request User Input node so playback stops for a point, distance or string at that step instead of replaying the recorded value.

parameters.name: ACTBASEPOINT
parameters.description: Records a base point so that coordinates in the macro are relative to a point picked at playback, making the macro reusable elsewhere in the drawing.

parameters.name: ACTMANAGER
parameters.description: The Action Macro Manager: rename, copy, delete and modify recorded values, and see the node tree of each macro.

parameters.name: ACTRECPATH / ACTPATH
parameters.description: ACTRECPATH is the folder new recordings are written to; ACTPATH lists additional folders searched at playback, which is how macros are shared from a network location.

parameters.name: ACTUI
parameters.description: Bit-coded variable controlling recorder behaviour: whether the Action Recorder panel expands while recording, whether a playback-finished message appears and whether playback pauses for input.

tools.example:
; Record a drawing-cleanup macro
ACTRECORD
  _-PURGE  _All  *  _N
  _AUDIT   _Y
  _ZOOM    _E
  _QSAVE
ACTSTOP
(name it CLEANUP, tick 'Check for inconsistencies when playback begins')

; Later, in any drawing
CLEANUP            ; the macro name works as a command
; or
ACTPLAY
CLEANUP
tools.notes: Action macros are a convenience for repeatable manual sequences, not a batch tool: they run only in an interactive session, have no branching or looping, and are stored per user in ACTRECPATH. Anything that must run over many files unattended belongs in a .scr script under accoreconsole, or in .NET. An .actm can be opened and inspected as XML if a recorded value needs correcting outside ACTMANAGER.

tools.name: acad.pgp aliases
tools.description: The program parameters file that defines command aliases - the one- and two-letter abbreviations experienced users actually type - and external commands that shell out to the operating system. It is a plain text file on the support file search path, with external command definitions first and an alias section after, each alias being an abbreviation, a comma and the full command name prefixed by an asterisk. Changes take effect after REINIT or by setting the RE-INIT system variable, without restarting AutoCAD.
tools.usage:
; external command
; command_name,[executable],flags[,*prompt],[return_code]
EXPLORER,   start explorer,  1,,
NOTEPAD,    start notepad,   1,*File to edit: ,

; command alias
; abbreviation,*FULL_COMMAND_NAME
L,    *LINE
C,    *CIRCLE
CO,   *COPY
TR,   *TRIM
XL,   *XLINE
-B,   *-BLOCK

parameters.name: alias syntax
parameters.description: abbreviation, one or more spaces, then *COMMANDNAME. The asterisk is required. Aliases for the hyphenated command-line variants are written with the hyphen in both halves.

parameters.name: external command syntax
parameters.description: Five comma-separated fields: the name typed in AutoCAD, the executable and its arguments, a bit-coded flag, an optional *prompt for user input, and a return code field.

parameters.name: flags field
parameters.description: Bit 1 starts the application and returns to AutoCAD immediately; bit 2 runs it minimised; bit 4 runs it hidden; bit 8 puts the argument string in quotes.

parameters.name: REINIT
parameters.description: Opens the Re-initialization dialog whose PGP File checkbox reloads acad.pgp into the running session.

parameters.name: RE-INIT
parameters.description: The system variable behind that dialog: (setvar "RE-INIT" 16) reloads the PGP file from a script or LISP with no dialog at all.

parameters.name: ALIASEDIT
parameters.description: The Express Tools command that edits aliases and external commands through a dialog and reloads them, instead of hand-editing the file.

parameters.name: file location
parameters.description: acad.pgp lives in the user's Roaming support folder (reachable from OPTIONS > Files > Support File Search Path, or with Tools > Customize > Edit Program Parameters). The first copy found on the search path wins.

parameters.name: conflicts
parameters.description: An alias that duplicates a real command name shadows it; a duplicated abbreviation takes the last definition in the file. Keep office additions in a clearly marked block at the end so they survive an upgrade.

tools.example:
; --- office additions, keep at the end of acad.pgp -----------------
ZZ,    *ZOOM
QQ,    *QSAVE
PU,    *-PURGE
TB,    *-TABLE
OF,    *OFGRID          ; a command defined by our .NET bundle
PDF,   *EXPORTPDF

; reload without restarting AutoCAD
REINIT            ; tick 'PGP File'

; or from a script / LISP, with no dialog
(setvar "RE-INIT" 16)
tools.notes: Aliases are per user and per machine and are not migrated automatically between releases unless the migration tool is used, so most offices keep a master acad.pgp on a network support path rather than editing local copies. An alias can point at a command defined by a loaded .NET or ARX module, but only once that module is loaded - the alias resolves at invocation, not at load.

tools.name: Design Automation for AutoCAD
tools.description: The Autodesk Platform Services service that runs AutoCAD Core Console on Autodesk's infrastructure, with no AutoCAD installation of your own. Three v3 REST resources model the work: an AppBundle is your packaged .NET plug-in, an Activity is a reusable definition of one engine invocation - the command line, the input and output parameters and any settings such as the script to run - and a WorkItem is a single execution of an Activity against concrete URLs. It is how DWG generation, extraction and conversion are run server-side at scale.

parameters.name: AppBundle
parameters.description: A .zip of a .bundle folder containing PackageContents.xml and your .NET assembly, versioned and aliased (dev, prod). It is loaded into the Core Console by the activity's /al switch.

parameters.name: Activity
parameters.description: The reusable recipe: which engine, which appbundles, the commandLine template, the named parameters (inputFile, inputJson, result) and their verbs, plus settings such as an inline script.

parameters.name: commandLine
parameters.description: A template built from $(engine.path)\\accoreconsole.exe with /i for the input drawing, /al for the appbundle folder and /s for the script that invokes your command.

parameters.name: WorkItem
parameters.description: One run. Arguments map each activity parameter to a URL - a signed URL from Object Storage Service, a plain HTTPS URL, or a data: URI for small JSON payloads - and outputs are uploaded with verb put.

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: The AutoCAD release the activity runs on, named in the activity and listed by GET /engines. Bundles must be built against a matching release.

parameters.name: nickname and aliases
parameters.description: Resources are addressed as Nickname.Name+alias (MyCo.UpdateTitleBlock+prod), which is what lets a new version be promoted without changing the callers.

parameters.name: onComplete callback
parameters.description: A WorkItem may carry a callback URL that is POSTed when the run finishes, plus a report URL holding the full Core Console log for diagnosis.

parameters.name: constraints
parameters.description: No GUI, no interactive prompts, no user profile, limited execution time and memory per work item, no network access from inside the engine, and .NET only - anything the Core Console cannot do, Design Automation cannot do either.

tools.notes: Develop against a local accoreconsole first: the same script, the same bundle folder and the same /al switch reproduce the cloud environment almost exactly and turn a twenty-minute upload-and-poll cycle into seconds. The script in settings is the bridge - it loads nothing itself, it simply types your command name, so the command must take all its input from files rather than prompts. The exact engine identifiers and region paths should be confirmed against the current APS documentation before use.

tools.name: Express Tools (BURST / TXTEXP / FLATTEN / BREAKLINE / ALIASEDIT)
tools.description: A library of small utilities installed with AutoCAD (full product, not LT) and implemented in AutoLISP and ObjectARX rather than in the core. Several of them solve problems that otherwise need real code, and because they are ordinary commands they can be called from scripts, macros and (command ...) calls. The ones worth knowing for automation are BURST, TXTEXP, FLATTEN, BREAKLINE and ALIASEDIT, alongside TCOUNT for numbering text, MOCORO for move/copy/rotate/scale in one command and the layer tools LAYMRG and LAYDEL.
tools.usage:
BURST      Select objects:            ; explode blocks, keeping attribute VALUES as text
TXTEXP     Select text to be exploded: ; convert TEXT/MTEXT into geometry
FLATTEN    Select objects: ... Remove hidden lines? [Yes/No] <No>:
BREAKLINE  Specify first point for breakline: ...
ALIASEDIT  (dialog) edit acad.pgp aliases and external commands

EXPRESSTOOLS   ; reloads the Express Tools menu and commands if they are missing

parameters.name: BURST
parameters.description: Explodes block references but converts attributes into TEXT carrying their current values, instead of reverting them to tags the way EXPLODE does. The standard fix before sending drawings to a consultant who must not receive live blocks.

parameters.name: TXTEXP
parameters.description: Explodes TEXT and MTEXT into lines and polylines so the lettering survives in systems without the font. Irreversible and vastly increases object count, so do it on a copy at the very end.

parameters.name: FLATTEN
parameters.description: Projects selected objects onto the Z=0 plane of the current view, optionally removing hidden lines. The usual rescue for 3D-contaminated 2D drawings before they go to a 2D-only consumer; run it in plan view.

parameters.name: BREAKLINE
parameters.description: Draws a polyline with a break symbol block at its midpoint, with settings for the symbol size and extension. Uses the brkline.dwg symbol, which can be replaced with an office standard.

parameters.name: ALIASEDIT
parameters.description: Dialog editor for acad.pgp command aliases and external commands that reloads the file when it closes, so no REINIT is needed.

parameters.name: TCOUNT / MOCORO / OVERKILL
parameters.description: Other automation-friendly members: TCOUNT numbers a selection of text incrementally, MOCORO combines move, copy, rotate and scale, and OVERKILL (now a core command) deletes duplicate and overlapping geometry.

parameters.name: EXPRESSTOOLS
parameters.description: Reloads the Express Tools menu and commands when they have been unloaded or the menu has gone missing after a profile change.

parameters.name: availability
parameters.description: Installed only with the full AutoCAD, English-language, and provided as-is rather than as a supported part of the product. They are not part of the core engine, so never assume they exist in the Core Console or in a Design Automation engine without testing.

tools.example:
; Prepare an issue copy: burst blocks, flatten, explode text, save under a new name
FILEDIA
0
_SAVEAS

C:/out/A-101_ISSUE.dwg

_BURST
_ALL

_FLATTEN
_ALL

_N
_TXTEXP
_ALL

_-PURGE
_All
*
_N
_QSAVE

; AutoLISP equivalent for the burst step only
(command "_.BURST" (ssget "_X" '((0 . "INSERT"))) "")
tools.notes: Every one of these is destructive in a way that cannot be undone once the file is saved, so run them on a copy created with SAVEAS at the start of the script, never on the working drawing. Because Express Tools load from ARX and LISP modules, a script that depends on them should check with (if (not (member "acetutil.arx" (arx))) (command "_.EXPRESSTOOLS")) before calling one.
